data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了中国在临床试验方面的快速增长。2017年，中国启动的临床试验仅有600多项，而到2023年，这一数字已接近2000。文章指出，中国政府通过一系列政策改革，如优先审查、有条件批准以及“默示许可”政策，加快了新药临床试验的审批速度。此外，中国加入国际人用药品注册技术协调会（ICH）后，接受海外临床试验数据，减少了在国内重复试验的需求。这些改革吸引了国际投资，推动了中国生物技术行业的繁荣。相比之下，美国的临床试验数量在2010年代末趋于稳定，而中国则迅速赶上。文章最后建议，美国可以借鉴中国的经验，以加速药物开发过程。

主要讨论点：中美在生物医学研究和创新领域的竞争与差异

不同观点：
• **[munchler]** 和 **[Veedrac]** 认为，美国在生物医学研究上的竞争力由于预算削减和政策问题正在减弱，而中国正快速进步，有可能引领新一波生物技术创新。他们担心美国的政策选择正在限制其竞争力。
• **[miki123211]** 指出，中国在人口基数和数据隐私上的优势使得其在临床试验上可能比美国更有效率。同时，美国的制度因对公众舆论和法律后果的担忧，可能导致研究效率低下。
• **[holoduke]** 强调中国在多个领域的快速发展，特别是其制造业经验带来的优势，并希望中国在芯片领域取得突破以挑战Nvidia等公司。
• **[pappyvanwinkle]** 为美国的生物医学和监管体系进行辩护，认为尽管存在问题，但该体系具有创新性和高标准，且美国在激励创新方面有丰富的经验和历史。他还指出，美国体系的优势不应被忽视。
• **[mmooss]** 认为，美国的保守主义正在限制其创新能力，政府和公众在创新上的滞后使得美国难以保持其领先地位。他批评美国在经济结构上过度保护传统产业，抑制了新思想的产生。
• **[monero-xmr]** 表示，如果中国取得医药突破，西方应立即窃取这些成果并使专利无效，因为中国不尊重美国的知识产权。
• **[buyucu]** 简单指出，中国在各个领域都在快速发展。
• **[nujabe]** 则悲观地认为，美国已经无法挽回地衰落了。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**在于中美在生物医学研究上的效率和竞争力。一些人认为中国因人口优势和政策灵活性在这方面更具优势，而另一些人则认为美国的体系具有更高的标准和创新能力。
• **讨论中提到的具体问题**包括临床试验的病人招募困难、数据隐私问题、政策激励机制以及中美在创新文化上的差异。
• **对保守主义的批判**也是一个重要讨论点，涉及到美国在创新和竞争中面临的内部障碍。
• **知识产权问题**也被提及，特别是如何在国际竞争中保护和利用科技成果。

China’s Clinical Trial Boom
In 2017, there were just over 600 clinical trials initiated in China. By 2023, that number was nearly 2,000. How can American companies kick off a similar boom?

In January, the Chinese company Deepseek released a reasoning AI model, called R1, that
performs comparably
to OpenAI's GPT-4o Turbo model on certain AI benchmarks but was developed with fewer resources at a much lower cost. Marc Andreessen called it “one of the most amazing and impressive breakthroughs I’ve ever seen,” even as NVIDIA’s stock plummeted by 17 percent — the largest ever one-day loss for a U.S. company.
While China’s AI competitiveness may have blindsided the tech world, the
pharmaceutical industry
has already had quite a few “
DeepSeek Moments
” of its own.
About
one-fourth of all clinical trials
and early drug development now happens in China. Large pharmaceutical companies in-license about a third of their experimental molecules from Chinese laboratories (meaning they purchase the rights to molecules developed by other research groups rather than discover them in-house), according to
a report
by Stifel. Just a couple of years ago, this number was about 10 percent.
"Ten years ago, a major [pharmaceutical company] seeking their next breakthrough molecule would have turned to an American or European biotech,” writes biotechnologist
Alex Telford
. “Today, they’re just as likely to license a molecule from a Chinese company. Chinese companies will often run the phase I trial in China for cheap, then flip it to a Western [pharmaceutical company] to run the expensive US trials and bring the drug to market."
The reason for this shift is due, in part, to policy. Chinese regulators have passed reforms that lower barriers to market entry and streamline approvals. Those reforms could hold lessons for U.S. regulators hoping to speed up drug development, too.
Sign up for Asimov Press. It will always be free.
Subscribe
Impacts from China’s reforms can be seen by looking at clinical trial enrollment data.
1
Such data is illuminating because enrollment numbers offer a measure of the administrative burden placed on new treatments as they move from concept to real-world testing. Patent filings and R&D budgets suggest how much a region invests in discovery, but clinical trial activity shows how projects navigate bureaucratic landscapes. By analyzing how enrollment rates respond to changes in policy, funding, and disease targets, we can see which approaches most effectively accelerate pharmaceutical innovation. Here’s what the data shows.
In the early 2010s, the number of clinical trials performed by American companies increased steadily but then leveled out at about 1,900 studies each year. China’s clinical trial numbers, on the other hand, remained relatively low until the mid-2010s. After the government
streamlined approval policies
, though, the number of clinical trials soared. Chinese companies matched the American clinical trial volume in the span of a few years while sustaining their average enrollment trajectory (at a marginally higher rate).
China’s jump in clinical trial enrollments doesn’t stem from a small number of large, late-phase trials (which would skew the mean), either. Rather, the
number of
original
,
new
drugs
originating in China has
climbed
from almost zero in 2010 to a figure, in 2023, that approaches American totals.
How did they do it?
Chinese regulators introduced several measures to speed up clinical trial approvals, including priority review and conditional approvals for new drugs. Drugs that qualify for priority review often address a critical, unmet clinical need, allowing them to go through an accelerated evaluation timeline.
In 2017, the NMPA (China’s drug regulator) also launched an “implied license” policy, which automatically authorizes a clinical trial if regulators voice no objections within 60 days. That same year, China joined the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) and updated its rules to accept overseas clinical trial data, reducing the need to repeat entire studies within China. This means that companies no longer need to repeat full trials in China if high-quality foreign results exist. Amgen’s
XGEVA
, a medication used to treat bone cancer, was approved in 2019 without further testing requirements based on a global Phase 2 study that included no clinical trial sites in China. Easier approvals and commercially viable results in multiple markets also led to
international investment
, which furthered the country’s biotech boom.

data.title: Duolingo will replace contract workers with AI
data.author: donohoe
data.article_summary: Duolingo CEO Luis von Ahn宣布公司将转向“AI优先”战略，逐渐停止使用承包商来完成AI能处理的工作。这一转变旨在通过AI消除瓶颈，让员工专注于创造性和更具挑战性的任务，而非重复性工作。公司计划在招聘和绩效评估中纳入AI使用情况的考量，且只有在团队无法进一步自动化工作时才会增加人手。Von Ahn强调，此举并非用AI取代员工，而是为了更好地实现公司的教学使命，迅速为学习者提供大量内容。同时，公司会提供培训和工具支持员工适应这一变化。这一决策受到Shopify CEO类似措施的启发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Duolingo的“AI优先”政策及其影响

不同观点：
• **对工程师工作影响的担忧**：Aurornis指出，Duolingo的内部公告暗示编码将变得不再重要，生产力预期却要提高，这令人担忧。强制要求开发人员在每个任务中使用AI，并通过大语言模型（LLM）来工作，而不是直接写代码，这种做法可能源于对LLM理解有限的非开发人员。Aurornis认为，这种做法不会显著提高生产力，反而可能适得其反。

• **Duolingo产品有效性的质疑**：n_ary和Larrikin认为Duolingo作为一个语言学习工具并不有效，它只是提供了一些基础的学习内容，类似于Anki这样的闪卡工具，但学习效果不佳。n_ary决定支持“以人为本”的企业，报名参加真实的语言课程。Larrikin则指出，Duolingo的内容过于基础，无法帮助学习者真正掌握一门语言。

• **对AI内容生成需求的质疑**：actuallyalys和SirensOfTitan质疑Duolingo声称的需要大量AI生成内容的理由。他们认为，创建学习材料主要是一个前期的任务，后续只需要少量更新和修正，不需要如此大规模地依赖AI。SirensOfTitan进一步指出，如果AI工具真的能显著提高生产力，就不需要强制推行。

• **对Duolingo未来发展的悲观预测**：iamleppert和boh对Duolingo的未来表示悲观。iamleppert预测Duolingo可能在18个月内消失，而boh认为“AI优先”只是掩盖 struggling business 的策略，实际上是通过削减人力成本来伪装成创新。

• **对AI在语言学习中作用的质疑**：nope1000和qalmakka指出，LLM在语言学习中的应用存在问题。由于LLM给出的答案可能看似正确但实际上错误，学习者无法验证其准确性。qalmakka进一步认为，AI应该作为人类的辅助工具，而不是取代人类技能，管理层对AI的理解不足，导致错误地将其视为可以完全取代人类劳动的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• **AI技术与传统方法的比较**：spunker540认为，尽管Duolingo目前受到批评，但未来新的AI辅导应用可能会超越它，就像Duolingo曾经超越CD和书籍一样。

• **Duolingo初衷的背离**：gs17通过引用Luis Von Ahn的初衷，指出Duolingo已经偏离了其最初提供高质量免费语言教育的使命。

• **Duolingo作为时间消耗品**：klipklop和xdfgh1112认为，Duolingo对大多数人来说并没有实际效果，只是一个浪费时间的应用。

• **相关替代方案的提及**：dang提到了一个开源的Duolingo替代品LibreLingo，供用户选择。

43827978.article_content:
News
Duolingo will replace contract workers with AI
The company is going to be ‘AI-first,’ says its CEO.
The company is going to be ‘AI-first,’ says its CEO.
by
Jay Peters
Apr 28, 2025, 11:47 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Duolingo co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn.
Photo: Getty Images
Jay Peters
is a news editor covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.
Duolingo will “gradually stop using contractors to do work that AI can handle,” according to an all-hands email sent by co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn announcing that the company will be “AI-first.” The email was posted on
Duolingo’s LinkedIn account
.
According to von Ahn, being “AI-first” means the company will “need to rethink much of how we work” and that “making minor tweaks to systems designed for humans won’t get us there.” As part of the shift, the company will roll out “a few constructive constraints,” including the changes to how it works with contractors, looking for AI use in hiring and in performance reviews, and that “headcount will only be given if a team cannot automate more of their work.”
von Ahn says that “Duolingo will remain a company that cares deeply about its employees” and that “this isn’t about replacing Duos with AI.” Instead, he says that the changes are “about removing bottlenecks” so that employees can “focus on creative work and real problems, not repetitive tasks.”
Related
Shopify CEO says no new hires without proof AI can’t do the job
“AI isn’t just a productivity boost,” von Ahn says. “It helps us get closer to our mission. To teach well, we need to create a massive amount of content, and doing that manually doesn’t scale. One of the best decisions we made recently was replacing a slow, manual content creation process with one powered by AI. Without AI, it would take us decades to scale our content to more learners. We owe it to our learners to get them this content ASAP.”
von Ahn’s email follows a similar memo Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke sent to employees and recently
shared online
. In that memo, Lütke said that before teams asked for more headcount or resources, they needed to show “why they cannot get what they want done using AI.”
Here’s the text of von Ahn’s memo from Duolingo’s LinkedIn post:
I’ve said this in Q&As and many meetings, but I want to make it official:
Duolingo is going to be AI-first
.
AI is already changing how work gets done. It’s not a question of if or when. It’s happening now. When there’s a shift this big, the worst thing you can do is wait. In 2012, we bet on mobile. While others were focused on mobile companion apps for websites, we decided to build mobile-first because we saw it was the future. That decision helped us win the 2013 iPhone App of the Year and unlocked the organic word-of-mouth growth that followed.
Betting on mobile made all the difference. We’re making a similar call now, and this time the platform shift is AI.
AI isn’t just a productivity boost
. It helps us get closer to our mission. To teach well, we need to create a massive amount of content, and doing that manually doesn’t scale. One of the best decisions we made recently was replacing a slow, manual content creation process with one powered by AI. Without AI, it would take us decades to scale our content to more learners. We owe it to our learners to get them this content ASAP.
AI also helps us build features like Video Call that were impossible to build before.
For the first time ever, teaching as well as the best human tutors is within our reach.
Being AI-first means we will need to rethink much of how we work.
Making minor tweaks to systems designed for humans won’t get us there
. In many cases, we’ll need to start from scratch. We’re not going to rebuild everything overnight, and some things-like getting AI to understand our codebase-will take time. However, we can’t wait until the technology is 100% perfect. We’d rather move with urgency and take occasional small hits on quality than move slowly and miss the moment.
We’ll be rolling out a few constructive constraints to help guide this shift:
We’ll gradually stop using contractors to do work that AI can handle
AI use will be part of what we look for in hiring
AI use will be part of what we evaluate in performance reviews
Headcount will only be given if a team cannot automate more of their work
Most functions will have specific initiatives to fundamentally change how they work
All of this said,
Duolingo will remain a company that cares deeply about its employees
. This isn’t about replacing Duos with AI. It’s about removing bottlenecks so we can do more with the outstanding Duos we already have. We want you to focus on creative work and real problems, not repetitive tasks.
We’re going to support you with more training, mentorship, and tooling for AI in your function.
Change can be scary, but I’m confident this will be a great step for Duolingo. It will help us better deliver on our mission — and for Duos, it means st

43828423.article_content:
An Illustrated Guide to Automatic Sparse Differentiation
In numerous applications of machine learning, Hessians and Jacobians exhibit sparsity, a property that can be leveraged to vastly accelerate their computation. While the usage of automatic differentiation in machine learning is ubiquitous, automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) remains largely unknown. This post introduces ASD, explaining its key components and their roles in the computation of both sparse Jacobians and Hessians. We conclude with a practical demonstration showcasing the performance benefits of ASD.
$$ \newcommand{\colorf}[1]{\textcolor{RoyalBlue}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorh}[1]{\textcolor{RedOrange}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorg}[1]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorv}[1]{\textcolor{VioletRed}{#1}} \def\sR{\mathbb{R}} \def\vx{\mathbf{x}} \def\vv{\mathbf{v}} \def\vb{\mathbf{e}} \newcommand{\vvc}[1]{\colorv{\vv_{#1}}} \newcommand{\vbc}[1]{\colorv{\vb_{#1}}} \newcommand{\dfdx}[2]{\frac{\partial f_{#1}}{\partial x_{#2}}(\vx)} \newcommand{\J}[2]{J_{#1}(#2)} \def\Jf{\J{f}{\vx}} \def\Jg{\J{g}{\vx}} \def\Jh{\J{h}{g(\vx)}} \def\Jfc{\colorf{\Jf}} \def\Jgc{\colorg{\Jg}} \def\Jhc{\colorh{\Jh}} \newcommand{\D}[2]{D{#1}(#2)} \def\Df{\D{f}{\vx}} \def\Dg{\D{g}{\vx}} \def\Dh{\D{h}{g(\vx)}} \def\Dfc{\colorf{\Df}} \def\Dgc{\colorg{\Dg}} \def\Dhc{\colorh{\Dh}} $$
First-order optimization is ubiquitous in machine learning (ML) but second-order optimization is much less common. The intuitive reason is that high-dimensional vectors (gradients) are cheap, whereas high-dimensional matrices (Hessians) are expensive. Luckily, in numerous applications of ML to science or engineering,
Hessians and Jacobians exhibit sparsity
: most of their coefficients are known to be zero. Leveraging this sparsity can vastly
accelerate automatic differentiation
(AD) for Hessians and Jacobians, while decreasing its memory requirements
. Yet, while traditional AD is available in many high-level programming languages like Python
and Julia
,
automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) is not as widely used
. One reason is that the underlying theory was developed in the AD community, outside of the ML research ecosystem.
With this blog post, we aim to shed light on the inner workings of ASD, bridging the gap between the ML and AD communities by presenting well established techniques from the latter field. We start out with a short introduction to traditional AD, covering the computation of Jacobians in both forward and reverse mode. We then dive into the two primary components of ASD:
sparsity pattern detection
and
matrix coloring
. Having described the computation of sparse Jacobians, we move on to sparse Hessians.
After discussing applications in machine learning, we conclude with a practical demonstration of ASD, providing performance benchmarks and guidance on when to use ASD over AD.
Automatic differentiation
Let us start by covering the fundamentals of traditional AD. The reader can find more details in the recent book by Blondel and Roulet
, as well as Griewank and Walther
.
AD makes use of the
compositional structure
of mathematical functions like deep neural networks. To make things simple, we will mainly look at a differentiable function $f$ composed of two differentiable functions $g: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{p}$ and $h: \mathbb{R}^{p} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$, such that $f = h \circ g: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$. The insights gained from this toy example should translate directly to more deeply composed functions $f = g^{(L)} \circ g^{(L-1)} \circ \cdots \circ g^{(1)}$, and even computational graphs with more complex branching.
The chain rule
For a function $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$ and a point of linearization $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, the Jacobian matrix $J_f(\mathbf{x})$ is the $m \times n$ matrix of first-order partial derivatives, whose $(i,j)$-th entry is
\[\big( \Jf \big)_{i,j} = \dfdx{i}{j} \in \sR \, .\]
For a composed function
\[\colorf{f} = \colorh{h} \circ \colorg{g} \, ,\]
the
multivariate chain rule
tells us that we obtain the Jacobian matrix of $f$ by
multiplying
the Jacobian matrices of $h$ and $g$:
\[\Jfc = \Jhc \cdot \Jgc .\]
Figure 1 illustrates this for $n=5$, $m=4$ and $p=3$. We will keep using these dimensions in following illustrations, even though the real benefits of ASD only appear as the dimension grows.
Figure 1: Visualization of the multivariate chain rule for $f = h \circ g$.
AD is matrix-free
We have seen how the chain rule translates the compositional structure of a function into the product structure of its Jacobian matrix. In practice however, there is a problem:
computing intermediate Jacobian matrices is inefficient and often intractable
, especially with a dense matrix format. Examples of dense matrix formats include NumPy’s
ndarray
, PyTorch’s
Tensor
, JAX’s
Array
and Julia’s
Matrix
.

data.title: Heart disease deaths worldwide linked to chemical widely used in plastics
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 一项由NYU Langone Health主导的研究显示，2018年全球有超过36.5万例心脏病死亡病例与塑料制品中常用的化学物质——邻苯二甲酸酯（phthalates），特别是DEHP（邻苯二甲酸二乙基己酯）有关。这种化学物质广泛用于食品容器、医疗设备等塑料制品中，暴露于其中可能引发炎症，增加心脏病风险。研究发现，非洲、南亚和中东地区受影响最为严重，印度的死亡人数最高，达39,677人。经济损失估计达5100亿美元，甚至可能高达3.74万亿美元。研究强调了全球需要加强监管以减少对这些有毒化学物质的暴露，特别是在工业化和塑料消费快速增长的地区。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料中化学物质（如DEHP和邻苯二甲酸盐）对健康的影响及其广泛应用

不同观点：
• **医院和医疗设备中的DEHP使用**：[hammock]指出DEHP在医院中广泛使用，尤其是在心脏相关的医疗设备中，如起搏器、导管、支架和瓣膜。由于DEHP的设计特性，它容易从塑料中渗出，这也是其提供材料柔韧性的原因。

• **BPA与替代化学物质的争议**：[DebtDeflation]提到过去推动"不含BPA"塑料的趋势，但制造商只是用其他可能同样有害的化学物质（如BPF和BPS）替代BPA，这可能没有真正解决问题。

• **通过补充剂减少塑料吸入**：[klevertree]介绍了一种名为NeutraOat的补充剂，旨在捕捉肠道中的塑料增塑剂，防止其进入血液，并提供了相关证据链接。

• **长期处理塑料后果的挑战**：[Havoc]将塑料问题与石棉相提并论，认为可能需要长达200年时间来解决塑料的后果。

• **对DEHP危害的广泛存在与担忧**：[KurSix]对DEHP的广泛存在感到不安，并指出365,000例死亡的数据突显了问题的严重性。

• **难以避免的塑料暴露**：[unstyledcontent]提到即使选择不含邻苯二甲酸盐的洗浴产品，塑料包装仍然会导致暴露，尤其是肉类和乳制品。

• **DEHP在食品中的含量**：[0xDEAFBEAD]提供了一个网站链接，可以查看哪些食品可能含有较高水平的DEHP，并指出在发展中国家DEHP问题可能更严重。

• **DEHP有害性已知多年**：[WithinReason]强调DEHP的危害性已为人所知至少30年。

• **去除生活中邻苯二甲酸盐的尝试**：[SomaticPirate]分享了通过选择硬塑料制品来减少邻苯二甲酸盐暴露的经验。

• **塑料与生育危机的关联**：[bhouston]怀疑塑料与食品接触可能是导致生育危机和自闭症增加的原因，并提供了相关研究链接。

补充讨论：
• **对研究数据的怀疑**：[dekhn]指出“关联”一词在科学研究中可能被误解，暗示需要谨慎解读DEHP与心脏病死亡之间的联系。

• **政治与商业利益的冲突**：[Hnrobert42]提到将此问题与美国国内对低出生率的关注联系起来的可能性，但同时对克服大企业利益持悲观态度。

• **研究论文链接**：[jiggawatts]提供了相关研究的论文链接，便于进一步阅读。

• **对研究结果的惊讶**：[0xbadcafebee]对研究中DEHP与心脏病死亡人数的关联结果表示惊讶。

Heart disease deaths worldwide linked to chemical widely used in plastics
by
NYU Langone Health
Credit: Unsplash/CC0 Public Domain
Daily exposure to certain chemicals used to make plastic household items could be linked to more than 365,000 global deaths from heart disease in 2018 alone, a new analysis of population surveys shows.
While the chemicals, called phthalates, are in widespread use globally, Africa, South Asia, and the Middle East populations bore a much larger share of the death toll than others—about half the total.
For decades, experts have connected health problems to exposure to certain phthalates found in cosmetics, detergents, solvents, plastic pipes, bug repellents, and other products. When these chemicals break down into microscopic particles and are ingested, studies have linked them to an increased risk of conditions ranging from obesity and diabetes to fertility issues and cancer.
Led by researchers at NYU Langone Health, the current study focused on a kind of phthalate called di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP), which is used to make food containers, medical equipment, and other plastic softer and more flexible. Exposure has been shown in other studies to prompt an overactive immune response (inflammation) in the heart's arteries, which, over time, is associated with an increased risk of heart attack or stroke.
In their new analysis, the authors estimated that DEHP exposure contributed to 368,764 deaths, or more than 10% of all global mortality from
heart disease
in 2018 among men and women aged 55 through 64. A report on the findings is published in the journal
eBioMedicine
.
"By highlighting the connection between phthalates and a leading cause of death across the world, our findings add to the vast body of evidence that these chemicals present a tremendous danger to human health," said study lead author Sara Hyman, BS, an associate research scientist at NYU Grossman School of Medicine.
According to the authors, the resulting economic burden from the deaths identified in their study was estimated to be around $510 billion and may have reached as high as $3.74 trillion.
In a past study from 2021, the research team tied phthalates to more than 50,000 premature deaths each year, mostly from heart disease, among older Americans. Their latest investigation is believed to be the first global estimate to date of cardiovascular mortality—or indeed any health outcome—resulting from exposure to the chemicals, says Hyman, who is also a graduate student at NYU School of Public Global Health.
For the research, the team used health and environmental data from dozens of population surveys to estimate DEHP exposure across 200 countries and territories. The information included urine samples containing chemical breakdown products left by the plastic additive. Mortality data was obtained from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, a research group in the US that collects medical information worldwide to identify trends in public health.
Among the key findings, the study showed that losses in Africa and in the combined region of East Asia and the Middle East accounted, respectively, for 30% and 25% of the mortality from heart disease linked to DEHP. Specifically, India had the highest death count at 39,677 deaths, followed by Pakistan and Egypt.
The larger heart death risks in these populations held true even after the researchers adjusted their statistical analysis to take into account population size within the studied age group.
A possible explanation, the authors say, is that these countries face higher rates of exposure to the chemicals, possibly because they are undergoing a boom in plastic production but with fewer manufacturing restrictions than other regions.
"There is a clear disparity in which parts of the world bear the brunt of heightened heart risks from phthalates," said study senior author Leonardo Trasande, MD, MPP.
"Our results underscore the urgent need for global regulations to reduce exposure to these toxins, especially in areas most affected by rapid industrialization and plastic consumption," added Trasande, the Jim G. Hendrick, MD, Professor of Pediatrics at NYU Grossman School of Medicine.
Trasande, who is also a professor in the Department of Population Health, cautions that the analysis was not designed to establish that DEHP directly or alone caused heart disease and that higher death risks did not take into account other types of phthalates. Nor did it include mortality among those in other age groups. As a result, the overall death toll from heart disease connected to these chemicals is likely much higher, he says.

• **塑料与生育危机的关联**：[bhouston]怀疑塑料与食品接触可能是导致生育危机和自闭症增加的原因，并提供了相关研究链接。

补充讨论：
• **对研究数据的怀疑**：[dekhn]指出“关联”一词在科学研究中可能被误解，暗示需要谨慎解读DEHP与心脏病死亡之间的联系。

• **政治与商业利益的冲突**：[Hnrobert42]提到将此问题与美国国内对低出生率的关注联系起来的可能性，但同时对克服大企业利益持悲观态度。

• **研究论文链接**：[jiggawatts]提供了相关研究的论文链接，便于进一步阅读。

• **对研究结果的惊讶**：[0xbadcafebee]对研究中DEHP与心脏病死亡人数的关联结果表示惊讶。

data.title: My sourdough starter has twins
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者参与的一个公民科学研究项目，名为“Citizen Science Sourdough Project”，由VUB布鲁塞尔和ETH苏黎世大学合作开展。该项目收集和分析了来自不同参与者的酸面团样本。作者的样本名为“Stinkie”，经过数年后收到了研究结果。报告从四个方面对比了样本：  
1. **双胞样本**：在瑞士、希腊和芬兰找到了与Stinkie完全匹配的样本，尽管气候和面粉类型不同。  
2. **发酵偏好**：Stinkie更酸、更轻，发酵温度较低。  
3. **酸度和年龄**：Stinkie的pH值为3.7，与平均值相近，但年龄为11年，远超平均水平。  
4. **酵母和细菌数量**：Stinkie的酵母和细菌细胞数量高于平均，尤其是**Lactobacillus brevis**细菌和**Saccharomyces Cerevisiae**酵母占主导地位，形成了一种单菌种培养，虽然稳定但风味单一。

研究还提到未来可能会有更详细的分析结果发布。此外，研究人员开发了一个名为Dough-Pro的AI助手，帮助理解数据。

43829935.article_content:
A couple of years ago, I participated in a study of the
HealthFerm Citizen Science group
in collaboration with the VUB Brussels and ETH Zurich universities. The study, called the
Citizen Science Sourdough Project
, aimed to collect and map micro-organism samples of sourdough starters with the help of citizens like you and me. As a sourdough bread nut, of course I was more than happy to send a sample. And then years passed and I completely forgot about the research project.
Until yesterday, when I finally received an email with the results of my sample (id
4f6d6
)!
In the first part of the result report, your personal sourdough starter is compared to all the other submissions, by investigating (A) possible “twins”, charted on a map of Europe, (B) fermentation preferences such as temperature and time, (C) acidity and age, and (D) amount of yeast and bacteria cells:
THe personalised result report, part 1.
Since the report is in Dutch, I’ll try to summarize it here for each of the four parts. My starter is called
Stinkie
—which does not really need a translation. When I don’t bake during weekdays, I keep it in the fridge, and I usually feed it rye at a 100% hydratation level meaning equal amounts of flour and water. This means it can get quite tangy and if not well-maintained, well,
stinky
!
Stinkie’s twins
—it looks like in Switzerland three other starter samples exactly match mine! Two more twins live somewhere in Greece and Finland. This is significant for me because the uniqueness of your starter is defined by the local climate, local flour, and the way you feed it to keep it alive. The weather in Greece is much warmer than in Belgium and Mediterranean flour is more nutty and
wheaty
than the ones I have access to, while the reverse is true for that twin in Finland where rye is more predominant than wheat. Perhaps they all use the keep-cool-in-fridge technique? Of course I’m just guessing here: the person maintaining his starter in Finland could just as well rely on imported flour.
Fermentation preferences
—compared to starters with rye meal, mine is more acidic and a lot airier (I sometimes feed it wheat flour), but weights much less. Compared to all starters, mine is kept at a much cooler temperature, and the bread I bake with it is much more acidic (when I can, I proof the dough in the fridge as well).
Acidity and age
—Stinkie’s pH level is
3.7
which is about the same as the average of all other starters, but the average age of all the samples is less than 5 years while mine is supposed to be 11 years old! That’s really cool and I have no idea how they measure that since countless amounts of refreshing must have thrown out and regrown everything?
Yeasts and bacteria
—Stinkie has about
41.69
million yeast cells per gram which is a bit more than your typical starter. I’m happy with that, more rising power! It also has a bit more bacteria than the average:
2.82
billion cells per gram. Perhaps because it’s older than others?
I wonder whether there’s a clear correlation between the last point and the age of the starter. I presume the researchers will be fishing for possible correlations and explaining these results in greater detail in some kind of publication I have yet to find (or is yet to be published).
The second part of the result report zooms in on the yeast and bacterial fingerprints of Stinkie:
The personalised result report, part 2. Bacterial fingerprint on the left, yeast on the right.
The graph shows five different vertical bars containing unique combinations of typical sourdough classes, with the sixth bar being the combination of your own starter. For the bacterial fingerprint, Stinkie most resembles class 3, although it looks like one particular species is completely dominating here:
Lactobacillus brevis
(
89.5%
). I think this has to do with the way I store the starter and the unique humidity/flour type/temperature we all use. I’d like to see a bit more variation here. No typical
San Francisco
sourdough bacteria for me…
As for the yeast fingerprint, something weird happened: it most closely matches sourdough profile 3, but even profile 3 has multiple species, with again one being very dominant. In Stinkie, however, there’s only
one
kind of yeast ever-present: the classic
Saccharomyces Cerevisiae
(
100%
). So while part 1 of the report says that in general there are more micro-organisms present in Stinkie compared to other starters, part 2 reveals that over the years, I somehow have been developing a monoculture? While this does produce consistent results and I know my starter’s behaviour very well, it would be nice to introduce a bit of variation in the flavour palette. I wonder what might happen if I was to feed it twice a day at room temperature for a month or so. How fast would that fingerprint change?
In case the results do not make sense, the researchers developed a multilingual AI assistant called
Dough-Pro
that will help you explore all the different aspects of the data. It sounds fancie

data.title: ArkFlow: High-performance Rust stream processing engine
data.author: klaussilveira
data.article_summary: ArkFlow是一个高性能的Rust流处理引擎，具有强大的数据流处理能力，支持多种输入/输出源和处理器。其特点包括高性能（基于Rust和Tokio异步运行时）、支持多种数据源（如Kafka、MQTT、HTTP、文件等）、强大的处理能力（内置SQL查询、JSON处理、Protobuf编解码、批处理等），以及模块化设计，易于扩展。用户可以通过YAML配置文件定义输入、处理管道和输出，并支持缓冲机制以处理背压和临时消息存储。ArkFlow还提供了详细的配置指南和多个示例，帮助用户快速上手。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ArkFlow项目的功能、性能、应用场景以及商业模式的讨论。

不同观点：
• **项目创始人的介绍与愿景**：
  - [chenquan] 作为ArkFlow的创始人，强调该项目是一个轻量级的分布式流处理引擎，旨在通过数据融合的生态系统和可扩展的能力，帮助社区降低数据处理的门槛，并相信流动的数据能产生更大的价值。

• **与其他工具的比较**：
  - [disintegrator] 和 [muffa] 指出ArkFlow看起来与Redpanda Connect/Benthos非常相似，并询问其错误处理和消息传递保证的细节。
  - [shawabawa3] 认为ArkFlow像是https://vector.dev/的简化版，主要区别在于ArkFlow使用SQL而不是DSL (VRL)。
  - [xyst] 则将ArkFlow比作Kafka Connect和Kafka Streams的Rust版本。

• **对流处理的教育与应用**：
  - [coreyoconnor] 提到在团队中推广流处理概念的困难，指出流处理对于构建弹性系统的重要性，但同步程序更容易理解，导致团队往往选择后者。

• **性能评估与质疑**：
  - [gue-ni] 认为“高性能”只是无意义的 buzzword，除非有基准测试或与其他软件的性能比较。

• **功能需求与建议**：
  - [jll29] 询问WARC支持是否在路线图上。
  - [insane_dreamer] 询问是否包括经纪人能力，并寻求推荐的云端经纪人方案。

补充讨论：
• **商业模式**：
  - [gotoeleven] 询问ArkFlow creators计划如何盈利。

• **历史讨论链接**：
  - [fer] 提供了一个以前的讨论链接（46天前），指向https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43358682。

• **简单的问候**：
  - [Uzoth] 只是简单打了个招呼“Hi bro”。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在ArkFlow的独特性、性能证明以及其功能的具体细节（如错误处理、消息传递保证、WARC支持等）。另外，如何在工程团队中推广流处理以及ArkFlow的商业模式也是讨论的热点。

ArkFlow

High-performance Rust stream processing engine, providing powerful data stream processing capabilities, supporting
multiple input/output sources and processors.
Features
High Performance
: Built on Rust and Tokio async runtime, offering excellent performance and low latency
Multiple Data Sources

Powerful Processing Capabilities

processing, and other processors
Extensible

43833310.article_summary: ArkFlow是一个高性能的Rust流处理引擎，具有强大的数据流处理能力，支持多种输入/输出源和处理器。其特点包括高性能（基于Rust和Tokio异步运行时）、支持多种数据源（如Kafka、MQTT、HTTP、文件等）、强大的处理能力（内置SQL查询、JSON处理、Protobuf编解码、批处理等），以及模块化设计，易于扩展。用户可以通过YAML配置文件定义输入、处理管道和输出，并支持缓冲机制以处理背压和临时消息存储。ArkFlow还提供了详细的配置指南和多个示例，帮助用户快速上手。

data.title: What Is "Induced Atmospheric Vibration"?
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: "Induced Atmospheric Vibration" refers to a phenomenon where extreme temperature variations cause anomalous oscillations in very high voltage power lines (400 kV), leading to synchronization failures in electrical systems. This effect, observed during a blackout on the Iberian Peninsula, results from atmospheric conditions like temperature and humidity affecting corona discharges around power lines. These discharges, influenced by environmental factors, introduce fluctuations in the electrical grid's reactance, complicating voltage and frequency control. The oscillations can lead to cascading failures in interconnected power systems, as seen in the widespread disturbances across Europe. Although not extensively documented, this phenomenon highlights the complex interplay between atmospheric conditions and power transmission.

The blackout seen today on the Iberian Peninsula

It's likely a cascade. The high temperature expands, stretches and distorts the cables (out of round), local heating creates 'thermals' (moving air pockets), the cable dance/gallop and touch. Short term interruption either trips a circuit, the load causes 'slowing' of the generators ('loss of frequency') or the transient short confuses a frequency monitor, and then more circuits are tripped off because of the low frequency (when low frequency the transformers saturate V/f with high peak currents) so more circuits trip. Boom; Iberia switched off!

Anyone who’s had to build a power system rapidly learns that electricity is not as simple as “electrons move, work gets done”.  Real electrical systems have to deal with issues of reactance and other exciting math-heavy constructs designed to drive you into some other field of study.
Power Grids experience this on an epic scale.  They have to concern themselves with a few needs simultaneously:
ensuring electrical potential doesn’t sag under load (maintaining voltage)
ensuring the integrity of the AC waveform (maintaining frequency)
ensuring the system doesn’t lose too much energy to fighting its own electromagnetic behavior (controlling the power factor)
That last one is the part that is profoundly nonintuitive.  Capacitance and inductance inherent to the system create a sort of inertia in the system that must be fought to provide those other two guarantees. Together they work to create what’s called “reactance”.
Long range lines and the equipment they connect to can have a lot of reactance.  High voltages make it even weirder.
One of the strange things that you don’t experience at lower voltages is “corona discharge”.  Very high electrical potentials cause the air around the conductors to become ionized.  When sufficiently ionized, this creates discharges.
You can see static examples of this natural phenomenon in the form of “Saint Elmo’s Fire”.  This often precedes a lightning strike if the potential difference is extreme enough.
But power transmission systems are not static.  They fluctuate dynamically with the AC waveform.  This causes situations where discharges or perturbation in fields that create them act as a new component of the reactance of the system.
Modeling this is very complicated and very important.  Real power transmission systems have active components that work to provide the above guarantees.  Most of the time, they are modeled well and tune things to keep the voltage and frequency where it should be with a minimum of losses due to reactance.
But these corona discharges are unlike the other two components of reactance, because they are affected by the environment outside of the system.  Consider… what affects the voltages at which ionized air molecules might cause a dishcarge?  Temperature and humidity do.
And now we finally reach the part where “induced atomospheric vibrations” starts to make sense.  When things get hotter or drier, discharges happen more readily.  And when they happen, they tend to happen at a given frequency.

data.title: Everything we announced at our first LlamaCon
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta公司围绕Llama模型的更新及其在AI领域的战略布局引发讨论，涉及开放源代码、技术细节、市场竞争和具体应用等方面。

不同观点：
• Blitzar认为Llama团队在Meta的元宇宙战略中幸存下来值得祝贺，但现在全公司全力投入AI，元宇宙的愿景似乎被搁置。
• Kennethologist详细列举了Meta在Llama模型上的更新，包括API预览、推理速度提升、生态系统扩展、安全工具和新资助项目，认为这些措施增强了Llama的易用性、安全性和社区支持。
• Mohsen1猜测由于Qwen 3的发布，Meta可能推迟了某些模型的推出。
• Throwaw12认为Meta正在进军AI云服务领域，可能是意识到仅靠社交网络难以保持领先地位，尤其是在AWS、Azure和GCP成功的背景下。
• Ahmedfromtunis质疑Llama模型在实际应用中的优势，表示尚未找到其相对于竞争对手的明显优点。
• Zoobab和Amusingimpala75批评Meta的“开放源代码”策略，认为其模型和训练过程不透明，存在“开放洗白”的嫌疑。
• Hedahet认为Meta在开放源代码方面做了不错的工作，但对其公布的更新列表感到失望，认为内容不够深入且缺乏具体数据支持。
• Wewewedxfgdf询问为何Meta不推出针对特定领域（如计算机编程）的模型，认为这样可以减小模型规模并提高运行效率。
• Nailer指出Llama的许可证并不符合开放源代码的定义，特别是其中的“附加商业条款”和广告条款。
• Andhuman对Meta未发布类似Omni的全能模型感到失望，期待能处理语音输入和输出的功能。
• Logicchains猜测由于Qwen 3的发布，Meta可能暂时推迟了Llama 4的发布以提升其竞争力。
• Scosman在尝试注册Llama API的等待列表时遇到技术问题，遭遇重定向循环。
• Havoc简单表示Meta的时机不佳。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Meta的“开放源代码”策略，许多用户对其真实性表示怀疑，认为其在开放性和透明度方面做得不够。
• 关于技术细节的讨论，如推理速度和模型更新，部分用户希望看到更多具体数据和比较基准。
• 市场竞争和Meta的战略转向AI云服务也是讨论的重点，部分用户认为这是Meta在面对其他云服务巨头成功后做出的必然选择。
• 实际应用和用户体验问题也被提及，如注册技术问题和对Llama模型应用场景的疑问。

data.title: Bamba: An open-source LLM that crosses a transformer with an SSM
data.author: shallow-mind
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了IBM Research在解决大型语言模型（LLM）推理效率问题上的最新进展。文中提到，随着对话变长，传统Transformer模型的自注意力机制会导致计算成本以二次方增长，造成延迟和冗余计算。为此，IBM开源了混合实验模型**Bamba**，结合状态空间模型（SSM）和Transformer的优点，显著减少内存需求，提升处理速度和准确性。Bamba模型能够在保持Transformer精度的同时，处理更长的序列并提高推理速度。SSM通过维护压缩的隐藏状态来减少内存开销，而Bamba等混合模型则利用了这一特性，同时保留了Transformer处理局部依赖的能力。文章还提到，IBM即将发布的Granite 4.0模型将包含Bamba的创新技术。

43835495.article_content:
Learn more about Bamba and see benchmark results in this
technical blog post
.
Join the first
vLLM meetup in NYC
on May 7 at the IBM Innovation Studio at 1 Madison Avenue in Manhattan! Hosted by IBM and Red Hat, the event will feature technical talks and discussion on how to optimize LLM inference for performance and efficiency.
The transformer architecture behind today’s large language models has shown an uncanny ability to generate human-like text. Part of its effectiveness comes from its self-attention mechanism, which allows the model to weigh all the words in an input sequence when generating a response.
The problem comes as conversations get longer. Because the model holds the running sequence in memory as it responds, the cumulative cost of generation grows quadratically. If the size of the context window doubles, the cost of processing the context and generating a response doesn’t just double — it quadruples.
This “quadratic bottleneck” is often behind that frustrating lag between asking the model a question and getting an answer. It also creates a lot of redundant computing. By the time ChatGPT popularized the transformer in 2022, researchers were already searching for alternative architectures.
State-space models (SSMs), and transformers interleaved with SSM layers, have emerged as two possible solutions. IBM Research has just open-sourced its first hybrid experiment:
Bamba
, a model that can run as quickly as an SSM and process long sequences as skillfully as a transformer. Many of Bamba’s innovations are part of IBM’s next-generation Granite 4.0 models coming in several months.
By significantly reducing the memory requirements of the transformer’s KV (key value) cache memory, Bamba-9B has shown it can run at least twice as fast as transformers of similar size while matching their accuracy.  “Everything comes back to the KV cache reduction,” says Raghu Ganti, the IBM researcher leading the project. “More throughput, lower latency, longer context length.”
The most important model you’ve never heard of
State-space models come nowhere close to matching the name recognition of transformers, but they’ve been used for decades to model dynamic systems.
“They are the bread and butter of electrical engineering — signal processing, robotics, and control theory,” says Ankit Gupta, an IBM researcher who has played a key role in adapting SSMs to deep learning. “Any field that uses time-series data would use state-space models to analyze it.”
The mathematical equations SSMs are built on can be applied to electrical activity in the brain, the weather, and even the stock market. From a series of observations, an SSM calculates a “hidden state” of fixed size, capturing the essential properties of the system. Think of the state as a summary of the past. When new data comes in, the hidden state gets updated, without increasing its size, along with predictions of what will happen next.
SSMs crossed over to neural networks in 2021, when Albert Gu and his collaborators at Stanford
released S4
, an SSM that applied state variables to language. Like the transformer, and recurrent neural network (RNNs), before it, the SSM was good at processing sequences of words. But it could process long sequences more skillfully than RNNs and much faster than transformers.
While a transformer attends to all the words in the context window when outputting a response, an SSM maintains a compressed hidden state that summarizes past information. This selective retention of information requires less memory overhead and leads to faster inference speeds.
S4 made a splash when it suddenly appeared on
Long Range Arena
, a benchmark for comparing language models by their ability to handle long sequences, but it was difficult to implement. Then an AI resident at IBM, Gupta helped Gu and team simplify the model using
diagonal state spaces
. Their “diagonal” SSM shrank S4’s 1,000 lines of code to 10. Gupta later helped to introduce
a gating mechanism
for filtering out irrelevant information, allowing SSMs for the first time to match the “expressivity,” or sequence-modeling skill, of transformers.
That team also unveiled what may be the first hybrid transformer. “Exploring hybrids made sense,” said Gupta, who now works on IBM’s
Granite Vision models
. “We could use standard attention blocks to handle text with local dependencies while leveraging SSMs to do longer-range contextualization.”
In 2023, Gu, then a professor at CMU, and Tri Dao, at Princeton, unveiled a gated SSM variant —
Mamba2
, which helped to inspire a wave of hybrids, with names like
Samba
and
MambaFormer
. Last year, Nvidia confirmed that these new hybrids could outperform either architecture on their own while dramatically
speeding up inferencing
, culminating in their release of Nemotron-H.
Overcoming the KV cache bottleneck

43835495.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了IBM Research在解决大型语言模型（LLM）推理效率问题上的最新进展。文中提到，随着对话变长，传统Transformer模型的自注意力机制会导致计算成本以二次方增长，造成延迟和冗余计算。为此，IBM开源了混合实验模型**Bamba**，结合状态空间模型（SSM）和Transformer的优点，显著减少内存需求，提升处理速度和准确性。Bamba模型能够在保持Transformer精度的同时，处理更长的序列并提高推理速度。SSM通过维护压缩的隐藏状态来减少内存开销，而Bamba等混合模型则利用了这一特性，同时保留了Transformer处理局部依赖的能力。文章还提到，IBM即将发布的Granite 4.0模型将包含Bamba的创新技术。

data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了电子前沿基金会（EFF）的各项工作和资源。EFF致力于保护自由言论、隐私、创新、透明度和国际安全等议题。网站提供了多种工具和项目，如Privacy Badger、Surveillance Self-Defense等，帮助用户保护隐私和安全。此外，EFF还参与法律案件、发布白皮书和播客，并鼓励公众捐款支持其工作。网站还提供了参与志愿活动和加入电子前沿联盟的途径，并展示了其在慈善评级机构中的四星评级。用户可以订阅新闻、行动和事件的更新，以获取更多相关信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对特朗普解雇Chris Krebs及随后针对其所在公司SentinelOne的行动的讨论

不同观点：
• sterlind: 澄清Chris Krebs和Brian Krebs的区别，指出Chris Krebs与KrebsOnSecurity无关，避免混淆。同时提到特朗普因Krebs声明选举安全而解雇他，并对其公司采取了进一步行动。

• spiderfarmer: 质疑在一个总统可以因个人恩怨而打击个人或公司的国家中经营企业的可行性。列举了一系列可能成为目标的群体和个体，指出政府使用过多惩罚手段。

• pr337h4m: 认为私营公司若要保持独立，就不应向政府或国有实体寻求业务合作，并表示近期事件使这一观点更加明确。

• apercu: 个人攻击特朗普，称其为懦夫，未提供具体论据或讨论事件影响。

• jeffrallen: 引用他人的比喻，认为政府的行动虽然是正确之举，但相对于需要解决的重大问题来说，效果微乎其微，如同用一茶匙水去扑灭国会大厦火灾。

补充讨论：
• 讨论了特朗普解雇Chris Krebs的背景及其后续行动对企业经营环境的影响。
• 涉及对政府使用惩罚手段的广泛担忧，以及私营公司如何保持独立性的策略。
• 对政府行动的实际效果表示质疑，认为其影响有限。

争议焦点：特朗普解雇Krebs及其对SentinelOne采取的后续行动是否合理，以及这种行为对商业环境和公司独立性的影响。

data.title: The last masters of Afro-Colombian machete fencing
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 巴西两位跨性别女性议员埃里卡·希尔顿（Erika Hilton）和黛安娜·萨勒斯（Duda Salabert）在申请美国签证时被标记为“男性”。希尔顿批评美国国务院的这一做法，认为这是对跨性别者身份的不尊重。尽管她们的巴西身份文件上已更正性别，但美国签证系统仍依据出生性别进行标注。这一事件引发了对跨性别者权利和身份认可的广泛讨论，希尔顿呼吁国际社会关注并改善跨性别者的待遇。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用 machete（砍刀）进行有组织战斗的传统及其与其他类似武术的比较

不同观点：
• CobaltFire 认为这个主题很有趣，但在 YouTube 上仅找到一个相关视频，显示出该内容较为稀缺。
• Pazimzadeh 提到这可能是“黑客新闻”中所指的内容，暗示讨论内容的技术性或专业性。
• Zonotope 将此与海地砍刀击剑（Haitian Machete Fencing）进行类比，提供了一个相关视频链接。
• Irq-1 强调保存传统的重要性，建议通过录制专家演示并使用现代技术（如3D和AI）来保存这种战斗体系，以确保其传承。
• Cs702 对此表示惊讶，特别提到无防护装备进行砍刀战斗的独特性。
• JBlue42 认为保持这种传统是有意义的，并将其与欧洲历史武术中的 Messer 战斗进行比较，提供了相关视频链接以支持其观点。
• 7thaccount 认为这与 Escrima（菲律宾武术）非常相似，暗示不同文化中相似武术形式的存在。
• Pmags 提出这种战斗形式与菲律宾武术 Arnis 的相似性，并讨论了西班牙殖民文化可能对这些武术形式的影响，提出了文化交汇或平行发展的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到与其他武术形式（如海地砍刀击剑、欧洲历史武术、Escrima、Arnis）的相似性和区别，显示出对跨文化武术比较的兴趣。
• 技术保存（如录制和使用现代技术）被认为是传承此类传统武术的重要手段。
• 争议的焦点可能在于如何有效保存和传承这类传统战斗形式，以及这些形式在现代社会中的实际应用和意义。

data.title: AirBorne: Wormable zero-click remote code execution (RCE) in AirPlay protocol
data.author: throw0101a
data.article_summary:
Oligo Security Research发现苹果AirPlay协议及其软件开发工具包（SDK）存在一系列漏洞，可能导致多种攻击，包括无点击远程代码执行（RCE）、单点击RCE、访问控制列表（ACL）绕过、本地任意文件读取、敏感信息泄露、中间人攻击（MITM）和拒绝服务（DoS）等。这些漏洞被统称为“AirBorne”，可能被攻击者利用来完全控制支持AirPlay的设备，包括苹果设备和使用AirPlay SDK的第三方设备。

其中，CVE-2025-24252和CVE-2025-24132两个漏洞可被用于制造可传播的零点击RCE攻击，导致恶意软件在本地网络中传播。苹果与Oligo合作修复了这些漏洞，并发布了更新软件。Oligo共报告了23个漏洞，导致17个CVE编号发布。

攻击可能影响MacOS、AirPlay SDK和CarPlay设备，特别是在设备设置为“同一网络上的任何人”或“所有人”时更易受攻击。攻击者可能通过公共WiFi入侵设备，进而通过企业网络传播攻击。
data.comments_summary:

Overview
Â Â Â
TL;DR
Oligo Security Research has discovered a new set of vulnerabilities in Appleâs AirPlay Protocol and the AirPlay Software Development Kit (SDK), which is used by third-party vendors to integrate AirPlay into third-party devices.
The vulnerabilities enable an array of attack vectors and outcomes, including:
Zero-Click RCE
One-Click RCE
Access control list (ACL) and user interaction bypass
Local Arbitrary File Read
Sensitive information disclosure
Man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks
Denial of service (DoS)
These vulnerabilities can be chained by attackers to potentially take control of devices that support AirPlay â including both Apple devices and third-party devices that leverage the AirPlay SDK.Â
The vulnerabilities and the attack vectors they enable have been named âAirBorneâ by Oligo Security researchers, as the attacks that they make possible are transmitted via wireless networks or peerâto-peer connections, and allow attackers to fully take over devices and use that access as a launchpad for further exploitation.
Oligo has demonstrated that two of the vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-24252 and CVE-2025-24132) allow attackers
to weaponize wormable zero-click RCE exploits
. This means that an attacker can take over certain AirPlay-enabled devices and do things like deploy malware that spreads to devices on any local network the infected device connects to. This could lead to the delivery of other sophisticated attacks related to espionage, ransomware, supply-chain attacks, and more.Â
Because AirPlay is a fundamental piece of software for Apple devices (Mac, iPhone, iPad, AppleTV, etc.) as well as third-party devices that leverage the AirPlay SDK, this class of vulnerabilities could have far-reaching impacts.
For perspective:
While not every Apple device worldwide is vulnerable to RCE via AirBorne, Apple stated in January 2025 that there are 2.35 billion active Apple devices across the globe.Â
In 2018 Apple indicated that there were over 100 million active MacOs users globally.Â Â Â Â
Other Apple devices like iPhones, Apple TV, vision pro are affected by different AirBorne vulnerabilities. Devices like iPhones require users to enable the AirPlay receiver in the phone settings.
Additionally, the number of third-party audio devices that support AirPlay can be estimated in the 10s of millions.
While the exact number of CarPlay-enabled devices is not known, it is widely-used and available in over 800 vehicle models.
Apple and Oligo have worked together to thoroughly identify and address the vulnerabilities with the goal of protecting end-users. Apple has released its latest versions of software to address the vulnerabilities and has allowed time for those devices to be updated. Throughout the responsible disclosure process, Oligo provided Apple with the relevant documentation, processes and code associated with these vulnerabilities.
Oligo disclosed 23 vulnerabilities to Apple in total, leading to 17 CVEs being issued. A complete list and description of these CVEs, as well as specific attack scenarios they enable, can be found below.
Types of Attacks
The vulnerabilities found by Oligo - independently or chained together - can enable a variety of possible attack vectors, including Remote Code Execution (RCE), Access Control List (ACL) and user interaction bypass, Local Arbitrary File Read, Sensitive Information Disclosure, Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks, and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.
For this document we have chosen to focus on RCE attacks on devices using MacOS, the AirPlay SDK, and CarPlay. In future posts, we may examine other types of attacks and other devices relating to AirPlay.Â Â
Remote Code Execution (RCE) Attacks
Using AirBorne, attackers can achieve RCE on vulnerable devices, based on certain factors, such as Apple and third-party device settings, as well as user preferences.
To provide examples, below are some of the different RCE attacks that are possible for devices configured with different settings.
MacOS - Zero-Click RCE
CVE-2025-24252
is a use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability that can be used as a UAF or manipulated into an âarbitrary freeâ action that enables an attacker to execute code remotely onÂ  MacOS devices.Â
When CVE-2025-24252 is chained with CVE-2025-24206 (user interaction bypass), it allows for a zero-click RCE on MacOS devices that are connected to the same network as an attacker with the AirPlay receiver on and set to the âAnyone on the same networkâ or âEveryoneâ configuration. The vulnerability allows for wormable exploits under these circumstances, given it enables an attack path that can spread from one machine to another with no human interaction.
A potential scenario: a victim device is compromised while using public WiFi, then connects to their employerâs network â providing a path for the attacker to take over additional devices on that network.Â

Oligo Security Research发现苹果AirPlay协议及其软件开发工具包（SDK）存在一系列漏洞，可能导致多种攻击，包括无点击远程代码执行（RCE）、单点击RCE、访问控制列表（ACL）绕过、本地任意文件读取、敏感信息泄露、中间人攻击（MITM）和拒绝服务（DoS）等。这些漏洞被统称为“AirBorne”，可能被攻击者利用来完全控制支持AirPlay的设备，包括苹果设备和使用AirPlay SDK的第三方设备。

其中，CVE-2025-24252和CVE-2025-24132两个漏洞可被用于制造可传播的零点击RCE攻击，导致恶意软件在本地网络中传播。苹果与Oligo合作修复了这些漏洞，并发布了更新软件。Oligo共报告了23个漏洞，导致17个CVE编号发布。

攻击可能影响MacOS、AirPlay SDK和CarPlay设备，特别是在设备设置为“同一网络上的任何人”或“所有人”时更易受攻击。攻击者可能通过公共WiFi入侵设备，进而通过企业网络传播攻击。

data.title: Jepsen: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17.4
data.author: aphyr
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL在多可用区（Multi-AZ）部署中的事务隔离性表现。PostgreSQL通常提供三种事务隔离级别：Read Committed、Snapshot Isolation（在PostgreSQL中称为Repeatable Read）和Serializable。然而，测试发现，Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL在多AZ配置下并未实现标准的Snapshot Isolation，而是可能提供了Parallel Snapshot Isolation，这是一种稍弱的 consistency model。

通过Jepsen测试库，文章展示了在健康运行状态下，RDS出现了G-nonadjacent循环，违反了Snapshot Isolation的原则。具体表现为事务之间存在非相邻的读写依赖，导致一种称为Long Fork的异常，而未观察到Short Fork（Write Skew）。这种行为在多个PostgreSQL版本中（从13.15到17.4）均有出现，表明RDS的多AZ集群无法确保Snapshot Isolation。

总结：Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL多AZ部署可能提供的是Parallel Snapshot Isolation，而非标准的Snapshot Isolation，导致在某些情况下出现事务隔离性异常。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL多可用区（multi-AZ）集群在Snapshot Isolation一致性模型下的表现问题，以及其对实际应用和开发者的影响。

不同观点：
• hliyan认为技术写作应更加直接、简洁，像STEM学科那样呈现结果，而不是使用网络流行语和复杂修辞。他表示过去喜欢阅读有趣的博客文章，但现在更倾向于简单明了的风格。
• luhn指出文章没有明确说明问题仅限于多可用区集群（multi-AZ clusters），这是一个相对较新的功能，与人们熟悉的多可用区实例（multi-AZ instance）不同。多可用区集群具有更高的健壮性，但其底层机制更复杂，可能是导致Jepsen测试失败的原因。
• havkom称赞了调查，并指出许多软件开发者对事务和事务模型的了解不足，强调这些知识对高流量和复杂问题的软件项目非常重要。他分享了自己在项目中切换到Read Committed Snapshot Isolation以解决锁定争用的经验。
• cswilliams提到自己曾在公司遇到使用pg_dump并行工作时出现的备份不一致问题，怀疑是否与本文讨论的行为有关。
• baq认为Jepsen的独立调查结果对RDBMS利益相关者来说不是好消息，并猜测内部会有一些担忧。
• ezekiel68分析了实际影响，认为在多可用区配置中，写后读可能返回旧数据，这是一种竞态条件导致的事件ually consistent现象，但不至于产生无意义的数据。
• nijave询问这是否是上游Postgres集群中的问题，或者AWS通过集群配置或补丁引入了这种行为。
• tibbar认为标题没有突出重点，应强调RDS for PostgreSQL 17.4未正确实现Snapshot Isolation。
• badmonster关心如果开发者假设Snapshot Isolation而实际上是Parallel Snapshot Isolation，可能引发什么样的安全或应用级错误。
• mushufulsa松了一口气，认为这只是长期存在的bug或功能需求，而非升级版本带来的回归问题。
• password4321希望所有Amazon RDS版本都能经过Jepsen测试。
• film42认为AWS需要更新文档以说明这一问题，并讨论了Snapshot Isolation修复是否会影响性能。
• oblio好奇Aurora在这方面的表现如何。
• wb14123对Amazon RDS未通过如此简单的测试表示惊讶。

补充讨论：
• 多可用区集群与多可用区实例的区别及其复杂性。
• Snapshot Isolation在多可用区配置中的实际表现和潜在问题。
• 开发者对事务和事务模型理解的重要性。
• Jepsen测试结果对AWS RDS用户的影响及AWS可能的回应。

争议焦点：AWS RDS for PostgreSQL多可用区集群未实现Snapshot Isolation的实际影响以及AWS应如何应对和沟通这一问题。

1
Background
PostgreSQL
is a popular open source general-purpose SQL database. It uses multiversion concurrency control (MVCC) to provide
three levels of transaction isolation
. PostgreSQLâs âRead Uncommittedâ and âRead Committedâ are both
Read Committed
. The âRepeatable Readâ level actually provides
Snapshot Isolation
, not
Repeatable Read
. âSerializableâ provides
Serializability
.
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
is an AWS service which provides managed PostgreSQL clusters. RDS automates provisioning, storage management, replication, backups, upgrades, and more.
Multi-AZ deployments
distribute database nodes across multiple availability zones, reducing the probability of correlated failure. RDS uses synchronous replication to ensure that transactions are durable both on primary and (at least one) secondary instances before acknowledging.
From a user perspective, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL provides a pair of URLs which speak the PostgreSQL wire protocol: a primary endpoint for read-write transactions, and a reader endpoint for read-only transactions. The primary endpoint supports all PostgreSQL isolation levels, while secondaries do not support Serializable. The strongest level supported across all nodes is therefore Snapshot Isolation (which PostgreSQL terms âRepeatable Readâ).
2
Test Design
We adapted Jepsenâs
test library for PostgreSQL
for use with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a
small wrapper program
. For each round of tests, we
provisioned an RDS cluster
using AWSâs
CreateDBCluster
API, using
gp3
storage and
db.m6id.large
instances. We then launched a single EC2 node to run our tests, and provided it with the main and read-only endpoints of the RDS cluster. We performed no fault injection, and triggered no failovers.
As in
our previous work on PostgreSQL
, our
primary workload
consisted of transactions over lists of unique integers. We stored each list in a single row, encoded as a
TEXT
field of comma-separated values. Transactions could either read a list by primary key, or append a unique integer to a list using
CONCAT
. This workload allowed our
Elle checker
to verify a variety of isolation levels, mainly by inferring dataflow dependencies between transactions and finding cycles in the resulting graph.
3

G-nonadjacent

data.title: Show HN: An interactive demo of QR codes' error correction
data.author: Xiione
data.article_summary: QR码具有内置的纠错功能，即使部分损坏（如边角被遮挡、撕坏或涂画），仍可被扫描。用户可以选择或上传QR码图片进行进一步了解，也可以直接扫描QR码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对QR码生成与纠错功能探索工具的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• [积极反馈 - 功能有趣且有用]
  ◦ [solardev] 认为工具很酷，并对最大错误率计算和可视化提出进一步的功能建议，比如增加最大可损坏像素数量的计算和控制生成时的纠错级别。
  ◦ [pveierland] 喜欢探索界面，但建议优化用户流程，让进入沙盒模式的步骤更易发现。
  ◦ [myself248] 特别喜欢鼠标悬停查看健康条与QR码数据位的对应关系。
  ◦ [gen3] 强调与QR码块交互和了解错误纠正机制的体验很好，并认为该工具在未来绘制自定义QR码时很有用。
  ◦ [teuobk] 喜欢通过调整位来观察块变化的效果。

• [建设性批评 - 缺少解释和UI问题]
  ◦ [flysand7] 认为工具缺少对QR码结构和错误纠正原理的解释，建议增加逐步交互式引导，比如解释QR码角上的小方块作用，并优化图标设计以提高辨识度。同时指出刷子和颜色变化的交互不明显，用户体验不佳。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：
  ◦ [flysand7] 提出工具虽然有趣但缺乏教育性内容，尤其是对不了解QR码结构和错误纠正的用户来说，交互没有明确指导。
  ◦ 其他用户则更多关注工具的功能实现与交互细节，并未提及教育性内容的缺失。

• 重要论据和例子：
  ◦ [solardev] 举例说明最大错误率计算和生成参数控制，建议通过设置不同纠错级别增加冗余。
  ◦ [flysand7] 提到图标难以区分，并用具体例子说明用户界面和交互设计的问题，比如刷子功能不明显。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：
  ◦ 用户普遍对工具的互动性和功能表示赞赏，但认为在用户引导和教育性内容上仍有改进空间。
  ◦ [flysand7] 特别指出，对于没有QR码知识的用户，当前的UI设计可能导致困惑，建议重新设计以提高可用性。

data.title: It's School time: Adventures in hacking an old Kindle
data.author: FlyingSnake
data.article_summary:
文章讲述了作者在一个周一早晨因女儿再次上学迟到而感到困扰，随后在浏览Hacker News时发现所有Kindle都可以被越狱，于是决定将家中的旧Kindle改造成一个显示上学准备信息的仪表盘。作者详细描述了越狱Kindle的过程，包括识别型号、安装WinterBreak、设置热修复、安装应用启动器和包安装器，以及通过USBNet包启用SSH访问。在解决SSH连接问题后，作者成功获取了Kindle的root权限。

接下来，作者介绍了如何在Kindle上创建一个显示自定义信息的仪表盘。利用修改脚本和命令，作者实现了在Kindle上周期性显示一张PNG图片。由于Kindle需要8位灰度图像，作者调整了图片格式并通过curl命令获取图片。

最后，作者设计了一个后端API，使用Cloudflare Workers、Hono JS、Cloudflare KV和Bun等工具处理实时数据并生成PNG图片，成功实现了仪表盘的功能。

43822251.article_content:
It was Monday and my daughter was late for the school again. To make things worse, the bus came early by 2 minutes. After rushing and making sure she caught the bus on time, I sat down for my morning coffee and opened up Hacker News. The front page had an interesting entry: “All Kindles can now be jailbroken”. Curiously my old kindle was lying next to me. Was this a sign from the universe? There was only one way to know and thus began my journey to turn my kindle into a get-ready-for-school dashboard.
Level 1: Jailbreaking the Kindle ⛓️‍💥
Jailbreaking the kindle was a relatively easy process. The fine folks at
kindlemodding.org
have created a user friendly guide with easy step by step instructions. The guide is very comprehensive and user friendly so it would be futile for me to repeat the steps here. The
KindModding Discord
community is also a great place to ask for troubleshooting.
In a nutshell the main steps I took to jailbreak my kindle were:
Identify your kindle model.
Install WinterBreak. (Just place the zip file in the kindle and reboot.)
Setup a hotfix, i.e. make sure the jailbreak persists after updates.
Install the Kindle Unified App Launcher and a package installer (MRPI)
Enable SSH on the Kindle using USBNet package.
Network shenanigans ☎️
I hit my first roadblock while setting up SSH access for the kindle. The standard USBNet package did not work for my kindle and after some research I found
USBNetLite
which got the SSH working.
The USBNetlite package enables connection to the kindle using 2 modes:
RNDIS/Ethernet gadget. This shows up as
usbx
(
usb0
in my case)
SSH over network using the IP address assigned by the router. This shows up as
wlanx
(
wlan0
in my case)
[root@kindle us]# ifconfig
lo        Link encap:Local Loopback
inet addr:127.0.0.1  Mask:255.0.0.0
...
usb0      Link encap:Ethernet  HWaddr EE:19:00:00:00:00
inet addr:192.168.15.244  Bcast:192.168.15.255  Mask:255.255.255.0
...
wlan0     Link encap:Ethernet  HWaddr 08:84:9D:7B:9C:F1
inet addr:192.168.2.71  Bcast:192.168.2.255  Mask:255.255.255.0
...
To enable the SSH network I had to do the following steps:
Enable USBNet from the KUAL Menu.
Set the IP address manually to
192.168.15.201
or any address in the
192.168.15.xxx
subnet.
SSH using
ssh 192.168.15.244
(usb0 ethernet interface) or the
wlan0
address assigned by the router.
Enter the password from the
/etc/config
file.
With this I had root access to the kindle 🥷
[root@kindle us]# uname -a
Linux kindle 4.1.15-lab126 #1 SMP PREEMPT Thu Nov 28 11:37:06 UTC 2024 armv7l GNU/Linux
Level 2: Conjuring a dashboard on the Kindle ✨
Kindle OS is stripped down version of Linux running an ancient kernel and old Gnu utilities but no package manager. The kindle has several custom tools that enable the Kindle UI operations, like the custom UI framework called
framework
and it’s side-kick
lab126_gui
. It’s workhorse is
lipc
, a
dbus
style program which is used to issue commands to drive the device operations.
There are several ways to develop an app for a hacked kindle. Some apps like KoReader use the FBInk framework
1
and some use Java applets
2
. I chose the easy path: disable the framework, display a PNG image periodically in full screen mode
3
.
I modified the main
dash.sh
script from the OG repos to match my needs. As it happens with old unmaintained devices, neither
xh
nor
wget
worked for my kindle in the background mode. After some debugging, I finally switched back to plain ‘ol
curl
to fetch the PNG from the backend API.
The script runs in a loop based on a cron schedules:
It stops the kindle UI frameworks and screensavers if they’re running.
It checks if the internet is accessible.
It fetches the PNG image from the server
It displays it fullscreen on the kindle using the
eips
command.
A Note about the image resolution: Kindle needs images in 8-bit Grayscale else it will not be displayed correctly. You will also need to find out the kindle’s display resolution using
eips -i
command. (Mine was 800x600)
I used a dummy image to test the kindle client before moving on to the backend side.
Level 3: The API server in the clouds 🌤️
I designed a backend API that collected the data in real-time data and exported it as a PNG image. For that I wanted a platform that’s always up, supports modern web standards, and has a pleasant developer experience. Cloudflare Developer Platform meets all the criteria and it was a breeze to get started.
I used the following tools/frameworks for my backend.
Cloudflare Workers: The workhorse to process incoming requests and image processing.
Hono JS: A Fast, lightweight JS framework.
Cloudflare KV: To cache network requests for an hour
Bun and TypeScript: I love Zig and Bun is really pleasant to work with.
Weather
I am a big fan of
Merry Sky
and the realtime weather API
Pirate Weather API
that powers it. After getting the API key, it was a matter of few hours to fine tune the data I needed to get current weather data. I loved that Cloudflare secrets make it very easy

data.title: The missteps that led to a fatal plane crash at Reagan National Airport
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：黑鹰直升机坠毁事件的原因及相关政策问题

不同观点：
• [keepamovin] 认为事故的主要原因是飞行员分心，并未遵循飞行教官的指示。根据录音，飞行员至少有两次未按照指示操作，尽管她看起来经验丰富且曾多次飞过该路线。该评论还提出了个人生活或职业生涯中的潜在问题是否影响了飞行员的表现。
• [firesteelrain] 关注陆军当时允许在民用空域关闭ADS-B Out的政策，质疑这种做法的合理性，尤其是在和平时期。
• [flowerthoughts] 对飞行路线的设计提出疑问，质疑为什么在机场跑道前有如此低的飞行路径，并认为在穿越机场时保持较高的高度可能更安全。
• [VirusNewbie] 质疑空中交通管制（ATC）为何没有与民航飞行员沟通，认为这是严重的失误。
• [listenallyall] 对飞行教官所说的“他认为空管希望他们左转”这一句进行了深入解读，认为即便飞行员幸存，她可能会辩称自己并没有收到明确的指令，因此需要自行评估情况，这与直接不服从命令有所不同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是飞行员是否明确收到了左转的指令，以及她未执行该建议是否构成不服从。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于政策的合理性，特别是ADS-B Out在民用空域的使用问题。
• 飞行路线和安全高度的设计也是讨论的重点，部分评论对现有设计的安全性提出了质疑。

data.title: What happens at the end of 'Trading Places'? (2013)
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: In the movie *Trading Places*, Louis Winthorpe and Billy Ray Valentine get rich by outsmarting the Duke brothers, two wealthy traders. The Dukes rely on a stolen crop report to trade in orange juice futures, expecting the price to rise due to a poor orange harvest. However, Winthorpe and Valentine steal the real report, which predicts a strong harvest, and give the Dukes a fake report saying the opposite. On the trading floor, they trick others into buying orange juice futures at a high price, while they have already sold futures at a high price. When the true report is revealed, the price plummets, and they buy back futures at a low price, making a huge profit. The Dukes, who bet the opposite, lose everything. This scheme inspired the "Eddie Murphy Rule," making such trading practices illegal.

Transcript
Feeling good.
Paramount/The Kobal Collection
hide caption
toggle caption
Paramount/The Kobal Collection
It's been 30 years since
Trading Places
came out. And, to be honest, I never really understood what happened at the end of that movie. Sure, Louis Winthorpe (Dan Aykroyd) and Billy Ray Valentine (Eddie Murphy) get rich, and the Duke brothers lose all their money. But what actually happens? How does it work?
I recently talked to Tom Peronis, a guy who has spent years trading OJ options. He walked me through every step of Winthorpe and Valentine's plan.
1. Give The Duke Brothers Bad Information
The Duke brothers — two old, rich guys — have bribed someone to get an advance copy of a government report on the orange crop. This will give them inside information on what's going to happen in the market for frozen concentrated orange juice. But Winthorpe and Valentine find out what the Dukes are up to, and they manage to steal the crop report before the Duke brothers get it.
Sponsor Message
The report says the orange crop is strong. When the rest of the world learns this, the price of OJ will fall. So Winthorpe and Valentine create a fake crop report that they put into the hands of the Duke brothers. The fake crop report says the crop was bad. The Duke brothers see this, and believe the price of OJ will rise.
2. Drive Up The Price Of Orange Juice Futures
The setting, the floor of the commodities exchange. The Duke brothers have told their trader to buy orange juice futures, and to keep buying no matter how high the price goes.
The market opens, and the Duke brothers' trader starts buying. Everybody else sees this and thinks the Dukes know something. Suddenly, everybody's buying. The price goes up and up and up, and the Dukes keep buying.
3. Sell To The Suckers
Then comes the key line for the entire movie — a line that's almost unintelligible. Standing on the floor of the exchange, Winthorpe (Dan Aykroyd) yells out:
Sell 30 April at 142!
Here's what that means: He wants to promise to sell orange juice in April for $1.42 per pound. The "30" in his line means he wants to start by selling 30 contracts. (One contract = many, many pounds of OJ.) (Also, that "30" might be some other number. It's hard to understand what he's saying. But it doesn't really matter — they sell a lot of contracts.)
Sponsor Message
All the other traders think the price in April will be higher than $1.42. The traders mob Winthorpe and Valentine, agreeing to buy lots and lots of OJ from them at $1.42 a pound.
4. Wait For The Other Shoe To Drop
A minute later, everything on the trading floor goes quiet. Everybody looks at the TV. On the TV, the secretary of agriculture walks up to a podium and reads the orange crop report. The guy tells the world that the orange crop is fine.
5. Buy Low, Get Rich And Bankrupt Your Enemies
To the traders, this means that the price of OJ is not going to go through the roof. All those traders who, a minute ago, were buying all they could, now suddenly need to sell. So the price starts falling. When the price hits 29 cents a pound, Winthorpe and Valentine start agreeing to buy orange juice in April.
In other words, Winthorpe and Valentine have contracts allowing them to buy millions of pounds of orange juice in April for 29 cents a pound, and to sell it for $1.42 a pound. They sold high and bought low. They're rich. The Dukes made the opposite bet and went broke.
Bonus: The Eddie Murphy Rule
One interesting kicker to the story: Trading commodities on inside information obtained from the government wasn't actually illegal when the movie came out, but it's illegal now. It was banned in the 2010 finance-overhaul law, under a special provision often referred to as the
Eddie Murphy Rule
.
Note: This story was originally posted on July 12. It was updated on July 19 to add audio from the radio version.

data.title: New atomic fountain clock joins group that keeps the world on time
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的科学家们推出了一种新的铯喷泉原子钟NIST-F4，其精度极高，有望成为世界标准时间的主要频率基准。NIST-F4通过测量铯原子的恒定频率来保持时间，其设计使其运行上亿年误差不到一秒。该钟加入了由全球十个国家运行的精英时钟行列，增强了全球时间的稳定性和安全性。NIST-F4不仅用于校准协调世界时（UTC），还通过无线电和互联网分发美国官方时间，广泛应用于电信、金融交易和交通系统等领域。它的推出标志着科学和工程上的重大突破，对现代社会的精密时间测量至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：原子钟及相关技术的现状与未来发展

不同观点：
• RetroTechie：对小型便携式原子钟感兴趣，提到以前曾有类似香烟盒大小的原子钟，但目前对超精确时间没有实际需求。他关注的是小型化、低功耗的原子钟，而不是大型、笨重的设备。
• geerlingguy：提到从铷原子钟升级到更精确的NIST-F4原子钟，并引入了核钟的概念，认为核钟可能带来更高的精度和稳定性。
• infogulch：详细解释了基于铯原子的原子钟的工作原理，并讨论了核钟的潜在优势，包括更高的精度和更窄的频率交互范围，同时提到核钟技术的实现难度。
• 0cf8612b2e1e：关注原子钟的同步问题，质疑在极高精度下如何避免在时钟同步过程中引入误差。
• algorithmsRcool：强调了时间测量的精度已经超过了其他物理量的测量精度，并引用了NIST的数据来说明光学晶格钟的超高精度。

补充讨论：
• CGMthrowaway：提到阿罕布拉宫的狮子钟，将讨论引向历史和文化背景下的钟表艺术。
• WarOnPrivacy：提供了NIST铯喷泉钟的解释链接，增加了讨论的技术背景。
• throw0101a：质疑时钟精度的“极限”在哪里，提出是否存在实际应用需要进一步提高精度，讨论了精度提高的边际效益。
• move-on-by：关注原子钟的地理分布问题，质疑为什么大量原子钟集中在一地而不是分散布局，提出了可能的物流问题。

争议焦点：
• 原子钟的小型化和实用性：RetroTechie关注小型、便携的原子钟，而infogulch和geerlingguy则讨论了新型核钟的技术可行性和未来潜力。
• 精度与应用的关系：throw0101a质疑更高精度的实际需求和应用场景，而algorithmsRcool则强调了当前时间测量的精度已经远超其他物理量测量。
• 同步误差问题：0cf8612b2e1e对高精度原子钟的同步问题提出了技术性疑问。

总体来看，讨论围绕原子钟的技术发展、实际应用和未来潜力展开，涉及小型化、同步、精度极限以及地理分布等多个方面。

NEWS
New Atomic Fountain Clock Joins Elite Group That Keeps the World on Time
April 28, 2025
Share
Facebook
Linkedin
X.com
Email
NIST scientists have published results establishing a new atomic clock, NIST-F4, as one of the world’s most accurate timekeepers, priming the clock to be recognized as a primary frequency standard — the ultimate source of time.
The NIST-F4 clock was carefully and painstakingly assembled and tested over the last few years.
By joining a small group of elite clocks run by a handful of countries, NIST-F4 makes the foundation of global time more stable and secure.
NIST scientists Greg Hoth (left) and Vladislav Gerginov work on NIST-F4, NIST’s new cesium fountain clock.
Credit:
R. Eskalis/NIST
Clocks on Earth are ticking a bit more regularly thanks to NIST-F4, a new atomic clock at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) campus in Boulder, Colorado.
This month, NIST researchers published a
journal article
establishing NIST-F4 as one of the world’s most accurate timekeepers. NIST has also submitted the clock for acceptance as a primary frequency standard by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM), the body that oversees the world’s time.
NIST-F4 measures an unchanging frequency in the heart of cesium atoms, the internationally agreed-upon basis for defining the second since 1967. The clock is based on a “fountain” design that represents the gold standard of accuracy in timekeeping. NIST-F4 ticks at such a steady rate that if it had started running 100 million years ago, when dinosaurs roamed, it would be off by less than a second today.
By joining a small group of similarly elite time pieces run by just 10 countries around the world, NIST-F4 makes the foundation of global time more stable and secure. At the same time, it is helping to steer the clocks NIST uses to keep official U.S. time. Distributed via radio and the internet, official U.S. time is critical for telecommunications and transportation systems, financial trading platforms, data center operations and more.
NIST-F4 has improved time signals that are “used literally billions of times each day for everything from setting clocks and watches to ensuring the accurate time stamping of hundreds of billions of dollars of electronic financial transactions,” said Liz Donley, chief of the Time and Frequency Division at NIST.
Introducing NIST-F4: The Nation's New Primary Frequency Standard
NIST-F4 isn’t just a clock — it’s the culmination of decades of scientific ingenuity, engineering breakthroughs, and an unwavering pursuit of precision. In this video, we explore the creation of NIST-F4, the United States’ latest primary frequency standard, and how it redefines what it means to measure time with atomic accuracy. From unexpected flaws to groundbreaking redesigns, this is the story of how one of the most precise timekeeping instruments ever built came to be — and why it’s crucial for everything from global synchronization to tomorrow’s technologies. Because when it comes to time, every billionth of a second counts. Find out more:
https://www.nist.gov/atomic-clocks
A Special Kind of Clock
Cesium fountain clocks such as NIST-F4 are a type of
atomic clock
— a complex, high-precision device that extracts timing pulses from atoms. These clocks play a critical role in our globally connected society: They serve as “primary frequency standards” that work together to calibrate Coordinated Universal Time, or UTC (an agreed-upon system for keeping time using data from atomic clocks around the world, known as a time scale).
National measurement labs such as NIST produce and distribute versions of UTC using their own time scales; NIST’s version, for example, is known as UTC(NIST). Those national time scales are then used to synchronize the clocks and networks we rely on in our daily lives.
Read more about how global timekeeping works.
In fountain clocks, a cloud of thousands of cesium atoms is first cooled to near absolute zero using lasers. Then, a pair of laser beams toss the atoms gently upward, after which they fall under their own weight.
During their journey, the atoms pass twice through a small chamber full of microwave radiation. The first time, as the atoms are on their way up, the microwaves put the atoms into a quantum state that cycles in time at a special frequency known as the cesium resonant frequency — an unchanging constant set by the laws of nature.

data.title: Path Isn't Real on Linux
data.author: max__dev
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了Linux系统中`PATH`环境变量的作用以及其查找可执行文件的机制。在Linux中，并不是内核负责查找`PATH`中的可执行文件，而是由shell（如Debian中的dash）负责解析和执行命令时进行查找。文章通过`strace`工具分析系统调用，发现`execve`直接执行带有完整路径的可执行文件，而shell在执行不带路径的命令时，会在`PATH`环境变量指定的目录中进行搜索。

文章还提到，其他编程语言如Python、Go、Rust等，在执行子进程时，也会自行在`PATH`中查找可执行文件，而不是依赖Linux内核。最后，文章指出，Linux内核并不处理`PATH`，因此在使用shebang时，必须指定可执行文件的绝对路径，像`#!/usr/bin/env python`这样的技巧则是利用`env`命令在`PATH`中查找Python解释器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux系统中$PATH环境变量的处理及其相关概念

不同观点：
• [mzajc] 指出，当文件在$PATH中但bash仍然报错说文件不存在时，可能是由于`hash`缓存了旧路径。解决方法是使用`hash -r`清除缓存。
• [blcknight] 强调，$PATH以及其他shell相关的功能（如路径扩展、管道、重定向、作业控制等）都是由shell处理的，内核不了解这些环境变量。
• [teo_zero] 对“$PATH由shell处理”推导出“在Linux上不是真实存在”的逻辑表示不理解。
• [wpollock] 认为，寻找可执行文件路径是shell的基本功能，内核不会参与这个过程。他还指出，这在Windows的cmd.exe中也是如此。
• [jakogut] 提到，Linux内核不处理共享库，这些是由用户空间的ld.so解析的。这种设计使得操作系统更具通用性和前瞻性。
• [inlets] 对“内核使用$PATH环境变量”的假设表示困惑，认为这是一个奇怪的误解。
• [drougge] 讨论了使用"#!sh"作为脚本解释器时可能出现的不可预知行为，尤其是当shell覆盖当前目录下的sh时。
• [cryptonector] 确认$PATH是由shell实现的，和所有类Unix操作系统一样，甚至包括Windows。
• [klysm] 建议更准确的说法是“Linux内核不知道$PATH，但shell知道”。
• [ashu14061] 提出，$PATH环境变量和其使用上下文是两个不同的概念，尽管$PATH和其他环境变量如HOME/USER相似，但其解释方式会因上下文而异。
• [taraindara] 表示，理解$PATH处理方式帮助解释了一些曾经遇到的行为问题，虽然不是严重问题，但理解后会更加清晰。
• [Tsiklon] 提出一个相关问题，过去是否更容易全面理解Unix系统及其组件。
• [SuperNinKenDo] 认为，作者误解了$PATH是由内核处理的，并指出自己通过讨论也学到了为什么在shebang中需要调用env来获得$PATH功能。
• [dfedbeef] 简单指出，$PATH在GNU/Linux中是真实存在的。
• [i140i485i765] 提到路径解析过程中的多个层次，包括VFS路径解析，甚至strace中的路径也可能被解析为另一个路径。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于对$PATH处理责任的误解，部分人误以为内核会参与$PATH的处理，而实际上这是shell的功能。
- 讨论还涉及到Unix系统历史及其设计哲学，比如将功能实现放在用户空间而非内核中的优点。
- 另外，有人提到路径解析的技术细节和不同情况下的不可预知行为，这显示了讨论的技术深度。

43838856.article_content:
PATH isn't real on Linux
​
On a fresh installation of Debian 12 (bookworm), executing
echo $PATH
shows the following output:
/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
/usr/bin
contains
/usr/bin/cat
, and
/usr/bin
is in
PATH
, so just typing
cat
will run
/usr/bin/cat
. But what exactly is doing this lookup?
By running
strace cat
, you can see the Linux system calls that are used:
c
execve
(
"/usr/bin/cat"
, [
"cat"
],
0x
7ffdfb2367a0
/* 63 vars */
)
=
0
The Linux kernel already has the full path (
/usr/bin/cat
), so where is
/usr/bin
coming from?
Reading the source
​
On Debian, shell scripts using
/bin/sh
use
dash
, which is responsible for interpreting and executing commands. Digging into
main.c
which contains the entry point:
c
/*
* Main routine.  We initialize things, parse the arguments, execute
* profiles if we're a login shell, and then call cmdloop to execute
* commands.  The setjmp call sets up the location to jump to when an
* exception occurs.  When an exception occurs the variable "state"
* is used to figure out how far we had gotten.
*/
// ...
static
int
cmdloop
(
int
top
)
{
// ...
for
(;;) {
// ...
n
=
parsecmd
(inter);
// ...
i
=
evaltree
(n,
0
);
}
}
evaltree
in
eval.c
is responsible for executing commands:
c
int
evaltree
(
union
node
*
n
,
int
flags
)
{
// ...
case NCMD:
evalfn
=
evalcommand;
checkexit:
checkexit
=
EV_TESTED;
goto
calleval;
// ...
calleval:
status
=
evalfn
(n, flags);
break
;
Then,
evalcommand
is used as the final step when the command is just executing a program:
c
STATIC
int
// ...
evalcommand
(
union
node
*
cmd
,
int
flags
,
struct
backcmd
*
backcmd
)
{
// ...
default:
flush_input
();
/* Fork off a child process if necessary. */
if
(
!
(flags
&
EV_EXIT)
||
have_traps
()) {
INTOFF;
jp
=
vforkexec
(cmd, argv, path, cmdentry.u.index);
break
;
}
shellexec
(argv, path, cmdentry.u.index);
// ...
}
shellexec
in
exec.c
calls
padvance
:
c
void
shellexec
(
char
**
argv
,
const
char
*
path
,
int
idx
)
{
// ...
while
(
padvance
(
&
path,
argv
[
0
])
>=
0
) {
cmdname
=
stackblock
();
if
(
--
idx
<
0
&&
pathopt
==
NULL
) {
tryexec
(cmdname, argv, envp);
if
(errno
!=
ENOENT
&&
errno
!=
ENOTDIR)
e
=
errno;
}
}
// ...
}
But what is
padvance
? Looking further into
exec.c
:
c
/*
* Do a path search.  The variable path (passed by reference) should be
* set to the start of the path before the first call; padvance will update
* this value as it proceeds.  Successive calls to padvance will return
* the possible path expansions in sequence.  If an option (indicated by
* a percent sign) appears in the path entry then the global variable
* pathopt will be set to point to it; otherwise pathopt will be set to
* NULL.
*
* If magic is 0 then pathopt recognition will be disabled.  If magic is
* 1 we shall recognise %builtin/%func.  Otherwise we shall accept any
* pathopt.
*/
const
char
*
pathopt;
int
padvance_magic
(
const
char
**
path
,
const
char
*
name
,
int
magic
)
{
The shell, not the Linux kernel, is responsible for searching for executables in
PATH
!
What about other code?
​
Python's
subprocess
can be used like this:
python
subprocess.run([
"ls"
,
"-l"
])
This calls
/usr/bin/ls
since
/usr/bin
is in
PATH
. But who's doing the path lookup?
CPython contains the following code for
subprocess
:
python
# This matches the behavior of os._execvpe().
executable_list
=
tuple
(
os.path.join(os.fsencode(
dir
), executable)
for
dir
in
os.get_exec_path(env))
which searches
PATH
directly in Python before calling out to Linux's
execve
.
Go is similar —
lp_unix.go
contains it's own implementation to search in
PATH
:
go
// LookPath searches for an executable named file in the
// directories named by the PATH environment variable.
// If file contains a slash, it is tried directly and the PATH is not consulted.
// Otherwise, on success, the result is an absolute path.
//
// In older versions of Go, LookPath could return a path relative to the current directory.
// As of Go 1.19, LookPath will instead return that path along with an error satisfying
// [errors.Is](err, [ErrDot]). See the package documentation for more details.
func
LookPath
(
file
string
) (
string
,
error
) {
Rust's
Command::spawn
eventually calls
libc::execvp
, which searches
PATH
:
c
/* Execute FILE, searching in the `PATH' environment variable if it contains
no slashes, with arguments ARGV and environment from `environ'.  */
int
execvp
(file, argv)
const
char
*
file;
char
*const
argv
[]
;
{
In fact, Linux doesn't know about
PATH
at all! Specifying a program in an executable text file using a
shebang
requires an absolute path:
sh
#!/bin/sh
works, but
sh
#!sh
doesn't. This is also the reason many programs use this trick:
py
#!/usr/bin/env python
print
(
'Hello world'
)
since
/usr/bin/env
calls
execvp
, which will search
PATH
.

data.title: Show HN: An MCP server for understanding AWS costs
data.author: StratusBen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS成本分析MCP服务器及其相关技术实践与许可问题

不同观点：
• **ponywombat** 提到AWS创建了自己的成本分析MCP服务器，并提供了GitHub链接。这表明AWS正在积极开发和提供相关工具以帮助用户进行成本分析。

• **_pdp_** 对生产环境中凭据散布在配置文件中的做法提出质疑。他认为这种模式可能会引发问题，尤其是在MCP服务器的示例中鼓励这种做法的情况下。这反映了对安全实践的关注。

• **mdaniel** 对特定实现方式（vantage-mcp-server）的工作原理表示疑问，并对许可文本表示质疑，认为其可能针对特定用户群体采取了限制性措施。这暗示了对许可协议和使用场景的潜在担忧。

• **andrenotgiant** 探讨了通过Vantage连接LLM与直接使用AWS成本和使用API的区别，试图理解不同连接方式的技术和实用差异。

• **cat-whisperer** 关注资源交织和标准化问题，询问是否能标准化处理不同资源的成本分析，还是只能根据情况个别处理。

• **salynchnew** 以讽刺的语气指出，云账单的复杂性曾被视为防止AI失控的保护措施之一，而现在只能依赖糟糕的IAM用户体验。这反映了对云服务安全性和用户体验的批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是生产环境中凭据管理的安全性，以及现有MCP服务器示例是否鼓励了不安全的实践（_pdp_的观点）。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对特定工具（vantage-mcp-server）的许可协议和使用场景的质疑，尤其是其对不同用户群体的适用性和限制（mdaniel的观点）。
• 技术实现上的差异和标准化问题也是讨论的重点，涉及到如何有效连接LLM与AWS API，以及如何在不同资源间实现成本分析的标准化（andrenotgiant和cat-whisperer的观点）。
• 最后，对云服务安全性和用户体验的总体批评为讨论增添了对更大图景的思考（salynchnew的观点）。
