data.title: A single line of code cost $8000
data.author: lordfuckleroy
data.article_summary: Screen.studio的屏幕录制应用由于一个漏洞，每5分钟反复下载250MB的自动更新文件，导致在一个多月内产生了9百万次下载和超过2PB的流量，给用户和公司带来严重影响。该问题源于代码重构时未停止5分钟检查更新的机制，导致应用不断重复下载同一文件。由于未设置云服务费用警报，公司直到信用卡被限制才发觉问题。最终，公司承诺承担所有相关费用，并建议开发者设置云警报、谨慎编写可能产生费用的代码，并添加强制更新功能以避免类似问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Screen Studio软件的更新机制及其引发的问题

不同观点：
• **支持开发者处理方式的观点**：
   - 一些人赞赏开发者愿意承担责任，并支付因软件错误导致的8000美元带宽费用。这种行为被认为超越了一般公司的责任范围，展现了积极的态度。（danpalmer）

• **批评更新机制过于频繁的观点**：
   - 多数评论认为每5分钟检查一次更新的机制是不合理的，建议改为每天一次或仅在启动时检查。这种高频检查不仅浪费用户带宽，还可能导致其他问题。（mieko, abstractspoon, spaqin, sevg, 999900000999）
   
• **对软件设计和测试的批评**：
   - 评论指出该软件缺乏基本的质量保证（QA），导致这种明显的问题未被发现。有人质疑开发团队的技术判断能力，并指出这种错误显示出开发过程中的草率。（jve, jarym, 999900000999, mgkimsal）
   
• **关于自建更新机制的争议**：
   - 有人建议使用第三方库如Sparkle来处理更新，以避免自建更新机制可能带来的问题。同时，有人指出过度依赖第三方库也可能引发长期问题，但在此情境下，自建更新器显然未达到预期效果。（gwbas1c, jmull）

• **对带宽和资源消耗的关注**：
   - 评论强调了这种错误可能对用户带宽和互联网资源的浪费，尤其是当软件用户量增大时，这种问题会更为显著。有人质疑如果费用被隐藏在免费套餐下，开发者是否还会及时修复问题。（albert_e, ValdikSS）

• **安全性和用户控制的讨论**：
   - 有人担心强制更新机制可能带来安全风险，特别是如果更新服务器遭到入侵，可能导致更严重的损害。（mimimi31）

补充讨论：
• **代码审查和质量控制的重要性**：
   - 一些评论强调了代码审查的重要性，指出即使是经验丰富的开发者也可能犯下导致严重后果的错误，如泄露个人身份信息（PII）。（donatj, jarym）

• **具体技术实现的建议**：
   - 评论中有人提出了一些具体的技术解决方案，例如在启动时检查更新，或在关闭应用时提示用户更新，而不是频繁地后台检查。（jve, jmull, mgkimsal）

• **开发者责任和用户体验的权衡**：
   - 评论反映出用户对开发者技术决策的信任度直接影响其软件选择，频繁的更新检查和未经同意的下载行为被视为对用户体验的负面影响。（mieko, jve）

通过这些观点，评论主要围绕软件更新机制的合理性、开发过程中的质量控制以及对用户资源和安全性的影响展开讨论。争议焦点在于每5分钟检查更新的必要性和由此产生的带宽消耗及潜在安全风险。

43829006.article_content:
TLDR
Due to a bug, our screen recorder app -
screen.studio
app kept downloading the auto-update file repeatedly, every 5 minutes for every single user. The update file is approximately 250MB. This resulted in
9 million file downloads and more than 2 petabytes (2,000,000 gigabytes)
of traffic on Google Cloud.
This screenshot might not look so scary at first, but take a look at the scale of it. For over a month, we generated at least 100Mib/s (a second!) and, at times, almost 1GiB/s of traffic (every single second!)
That bug was painfully simple and stupid.
Screen Studio is a screen recorder for macOS. It is desktop app. It means we need some auto-updater to allow users to install the latest app version easily.
The app checks for the update every 5 minutes or when the user activates the app.
Normally, when the app detected the update - it downloaded it and stopped the 5 minutes interval until the user installed it and restarted it.
Tragic refactor
The problem with the auto-updater we had was that it would prompt the user to update the app as soon as it became available. This resulted in a popup appearing while users were recording the screen, which obviously provided a bad experience as it interrupted the recording the user was making.
While refactoring it,
I forgot to add the code to stop the 5-minute interval after the new version file was available and downloaded.
It meant
the app was downloading the same 250MB file, over and over again, every 5 minutes.
Tragic context - app running in the background for weeks
It turns out thousands of our users had the app running in the background, even though they were not using it or checking it
for weeks
(!). It meant thousands of users had auto-updater constantly running and downloading the new version file (250MB) over and over again every 5 minutes
The math
Let’s do some quick math here.
Doing something every 5 minutes means doing it approximately
288 times a day
.
The update file is about 250 MB, meaning
72 GB of downloads per user daily
.
We had this situation happening for
over a month before we noticed it
.
We had at least a
thousand such app instances running
in the background at any moment.
250 MB * 288 downloads per day * 30 days * 1000 users:
It means it was roughly:
2 000 000 gigabytes,
or 2 000 terabytes
or 2 petabytes of traffic.
Series of bad mistakes
We did not have cost alerts on Google Cloud
. Before this situation occurred, we were paying at most $300 a month.
We were also not regularly checking the situation as it just worked.
We noticed it because my credit card started to block the transaction due to limits I had set on it (lucky me!).
Consequences for the users
It was not only bad for us but even worse for some of the users.
As mentioned, the app was generating so much traffic.
It means it was their machine generating network traffic on their home router and their internet provider.
One of our users, who lived in a house, had their internet provider cancel their contract due to enormous traffic generated during a month. It was extremely problematic as there was no other internet provider available around.
We decided to take responsibility and offer to cover all the costs related to this situation.
Luckily, it was not needed as the person could figure out the situation with the provider without bigger problems.
That was, however, quite a terrible experience for that person and me. As a designer, I value the experience product I create provides to the users. And this was not even a bad experience; it was actually harmful.
Summarising
Set alerts
on your cloud at all times.
Write your auto-updater code very carefully.
Actually,
write any code that has the potential to generate costs carefully
.
Add special signals you can change on your server, which the app will understand, such as a
forced update
that will install without asking the user.
Regularly check your cloud.
43829006.article_summary: Screen.studio的屏幕录制应用由于一个漏洞，每5分钟反复下载250MB的自动更新文件，导致在一个多月内产生了9百万次下载和超过2PB的流量，给用户和公司带来严重影响。该问题源于代码重构时未停止5分钟检查更新的机制，导致应用不断重复下载同一文件。由于未设置云服务费用警报，公司直到信用卡被限制才发觉问题。最终，公司承诺承担所有相关费用，并建议开发者设置云警报、谨慎编写可能产生费用的代码，并添加强制更新功能以避免类似问题。

• **批评更新机制过于频繁的观点**：
   - 多数评论认为每5分钟检查一次更新的机制是不合理的，建议改为每天一次或仅在启动时检查。这种高频检查不仅浪费用户带宽，还可能导致其他问题。（mieko, abstractspoon, spaqin, sevg, 999900000999）
   
• **对软件设计和测试的批评**：
   - 评论指出该软件缺乏基本的质量保证（QA），导致这种明显的问题未被发现。有人质疑开发团队的技术判断能力，并指出这种错误显示出开发过程中的草率。（jve, jarym, 999900000999, mgkimsal）
   
• **关于自建更新机制的争议**：
   - 有人建议使用第三方库如Sparkle来处理更新，以避免自建更新机制可能带来的问题。同时，有人指出过度依赖第三方库也可能引发长期问题，但在此情境下，自建更新器显然未达到预期效果。（gwbas1c, jmull）

• **对带宽和资源消耗的关注**：
   - 评论强调了这种错误可能对用户带宽和互联网资源的浪费，尤其是当软件用户量增大时，这种问题会更为显著。有人质疑如果费用被隐藏在免费套餐下，开发者是否还会及时修复问题。（albert_e, ValdikSS）

• **安全性和用户控制的讨论**：
   - 有人担心强制更新机制可能带来安全风险，特别是如果更新服务器遭到入侵，可能导致更严重的损害。（mimimi31）

补充讨论：
• **代码审查和质量控制的重要性**：
   - 一些评论强调了代码审查的重要性，指出即使是经验丰富的开发者也可能犯下导致严重后果的错误，如泄露个人身份信息（PII）。（donatj, jarym）

• **具体技术实现的建议**：
   - 评论中有人提出了一些具体的技术解决方案，例如在启动时检查更新，或在关闭应用时提示用户更新，而不是频繁地后台检查。（jve, jmull, mgkimsal）

• **开发者责任和用户体验的权衡**：
   - 评论反映出用户对开发者技术决策的信任度直接影响其软件选择，频繁的更新检查和未经同意的下载行为被视为对用户体验的负面影响。（mieko, jve）

通过这些观点，评论主要围绕软件更新机制的合理性、开发过程中的质量控制以及对用户资源和安全性的影响展开讨论。争议焦点在于每5分钟检查更新的必要性和由此产生的带宽消耗及潜在安全风险。

data.title: The Cybertruck is all tricks and no truck, a musky Tesla fail
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 这篇文章尖锐批评了特斯拉的Cybertruck，称其设计拙劣、功能缺失，不仅在物理上存在安全隐患，还因其与特定政治人物和意识形态的关联，成为了一种负面象征。文章嘲讽了Cybertruck的外观和性能，指出它无法胜任传统皮卡的工作，如搬运、建筑和越野等，反而成为了“浅薄男子气概”和“法西斯帝国主义”的代表。同时，文章提到Cybertruck在美洲原住民土地上的销售，批评这些车辆只是占用空间，并未回馈土地。最终，作者表达了对传统皮卡所代表的工作生活平衡和社区建设的怀念。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [文化视角] cafard从文化角度分析，认为卡车象征着工作与生活的平衡，是技术工人的交通工具，但质疑城市居民对大马力卡车的实际需求。
• [技术视角] testing22321对Tesla的技术创新持肯定态度，认为其在简化车辆线路和电子系统方面的努力值得肯定，并对未来车型抱有期待，但也指出Elon Musk的言论不可全信。
• [讽刺观点] Improvement用讽刺的语气形容Tesla的Cybertruck像在 dysfunctional men 的聚集地行驶，暗示其设计和市场定位有问题。
• [现实观察] Clubber观察到Cybertrucks在其居住地很常见，认为其外观具有未来感，受到了当地居民的欢迎。
• [政治视角] bboygravity认为对Musk和Tesla的批评部分源于政治立场，暗示这些批评可能带有偏见。
• [实用比较] MarkusWandel通过对比旧款卡车的耐用性，认为Cybertruck的坚固性超出预期，但也指出现代卡车逐渐转变为高价 passenger vehicles，失去了传统的实用性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对Cybertruck的外观和实用性存在不同看法，有人认为其未来感强，受到欢迎，但也有人质疑其设计和市场定位。
• Tesla的利润来源和财务状况成为讨论焦点，特别是出售排放信用额度的利润贡献被认为是不可持续的。
• 对Elon Musk的言论和领导能力的评价存在分歧，有人持怀疑态度，有人则抱有期待。
• 对现代卡车功能和传统卡车实用性的比较，反映出对汽车工业发展方向的不同看法。

You, Cybertruck, are not just repulsive; you are comical. It’s not your fault that you’re not really a truck. But if your operating system is listening, I have to tell you: You are the dumbest vehicle ever engineered.
Your sleek, commercial kitchen-shaped exterior, which is called a “cantrail,” can’t even stay on: It peels off your body at high speeds when the glue holding it together malfunctions. It lives up to its name, because, in so many ways, this car just
can’t.
You and the other 46,906 Cybertrucks manufactured since 2023 have been ordered off American highways for immediate repair. You are a road hazard, a danger to other drivers.
In ordinary circumstances, we would just laugh at you. And I do laugh when I think about the head of the FBI driving to work each morning in a custom-wrapped Cybertruck barely held together by inadequate glue.
At perhaps any other time in U.S. history, you’d have fallen into obscurity as the not-truck you are, a silly thing promoted by an eccentric billionaire crypto bro with a predilection for ketamine. But that billionaire car dealer is currently running around the White House gutting federal agencies and throwing out Hitler salutes. Now every white supremacist or men’s rights advocate with a crypto exchange key wants a Cybertruck in their driveway. You’ve become a symbol, the dead end where bad men drive deeper into dysfunction, shallow masculinity and toxic American disposability.
You are the carpool that ferries toxic waste from around the world into Texas to be glued together with shiny materials and stamped “American Made.”
But to anyone with a job that requires a functioning truck, the Cybertruck is a monstrosity. It cannot haul, lift, climb or build. At its core, it simply does not truck. Most egregiously, it voids the deeper truck experience, severing the vital connections that bond truck-driving humans: wood hauls, fishing and camping trips. Mudding, modding, racing. Cruising in a clean Chevy to Tom Petty’s “Free Fallin’” in the tape deck.
You are the carpool that ferries toxic waste from around the world into Texas to be glued together with shiny materials and stamped “American Made.”
At its best, a truck celebrates work-life balance. It is the vehicle of skilled labor. That’s what drives so many truck owners: building and strengthening communities, creating legacies, forging connections. That’s why we spend hours tinkering with that long-bed four-wheel-drive in the backyard. A little more oil, one more crank, one last job before an adventure down the back roads, where perhaps this time you’ll go farther than before.
The Cybertruck, because of that billionaire’s politics, is a clearly identifiable symbol of a more infantile masculinity and a badge of fascist imperialism, less a truck than an elaborate performance of a truck that gets stuck in snow and stranded on hillsides, trapped in mud, greeted by raised middle fingers and sprayed with graffiti across the country.
“Motherfucker,”
I say to its silver rear bumper. I want to flip it off, to toss cockroach poison at it. This metallic lump of excrement needs to be flushed. As many already have: In Las Vegas and Kansas City, Tesla dealerships have been vandalized and Cybertrucks burned, even though the White House has decreed that flushing a Tesla is an act of domestic terrorism.
Outside my hometown, Albuquerque, where the city ends and modular suburban homes climb the hill toward the Santa Fe National Forest, there’s a Tesla sales lot, filled with a fleet of the angular silver Nazi Wagons.
Credit:
Antoine Maillard/High Country News
There is a painful irony here: That lot sits on Tamaya, on sovereign land with its own sovereign business practices. New Mexico state law prohibits direct car sales from manufacturers, so those trucks would be illegal to sell if the shop was across the street. But this is America 2025, and inventive tribes have learned to leverage money and law. So Santa Ana Pueblo approved its own car sales law, and Tamaya Enterprises, its business arm, arranged a lease with the company. This also happened in Nambé, where a tribe just outside Santa Fe and Los Alamos has a similar deal. Cybertrucks are sold on tribal land, but they are not in spaces that Native people, or any real truck people, go. They are simply taking our space.
My Indigenous upbringing taught me to give back to this land, which belongs to my ancestors. That value is real and spiritual for me; I remember where I came from. But these cyber-things are made of rare minerals extracted from the land. They give nothing back, only take.
I want a truck for the memories it creates, cold mornings gripping a warm burrito in the tiny back seat on the way to a worksite with my uncles. On th

data.title: Show HN: Web-eval-agent – Let the coding agent debug itself
data.author: neversettles
data.article_summary: **Operative-Sh/web-eval-agent** 是一个自主评估和调试网页应用的MCP服务器。通过BrowserUse技术，它能自动导航网页、捕获网络流量、收集控制台错误，并进行端到端代码测试。该工具使用Playwright实现自主调试，支持macOS/Linux快速启动，并提供手动Windows安装指南。用户可以通过API key调用web-eval-agent，并在代码编辑器中查看评估报告和日志。该项目基于Apache-2.0许可证，主要使用Python开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码工具的效率、实用性及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **proc0**：认为该AI编码工具虽然方向正确，但完成简单任务需要大量步骤和输出，可能在处理更复杂任务时面临性能挑战，质疑其可扩展性。
• **klntsky**：基于自身经验，认为该工具与手动操作相比并没有增加太多额外的价值，因为通过其他方式（如windsurf）也能实现类似结果，只是需要一些人工输入。
• **esafak**：关注该工具的性能和效率，建议或呼吁建立一个基准（或通过社区众包方式）来衡量其表现，以帮助用户评估其实际效果。
• **gitroom**：非常支持该工具，认为它能有效减少手动点击和检查等重复性工作，从而节省时间，提升工作效率。
• **nico**：对工具表示赞赏，但同时提出问题，询问该工具与浏览器MCP（https://browsermcp.io/）的区别和优劣。
• **GreenGames**：对工具表示赞赏，但提出一个具体的技术问题，关心该工具在多步骤任务中是否能自动保存cookies/localStorage，还是需要手动编写认证脚本。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是该AI工具是否真正提升了工作效率，特别是在处理复杂任务时的性能表现。**proc0**和**klntsky**对其实际效用有所保留，而**gitroom**则认为工具在减少手动操作方面有显著优势。
• 另一个讨论点是工具的功能细节，如**nico**和**GreenGames**都提到了与其他工具的比较及技术实现问题，特别是关于认证和数据保存的自动化程度。
• **esafak**提出了建立基准的建议，这可能对整个社区评估该类工具的实际性能和效率有帮助。

• **gitroom**：非常支持该工具，认为它能有效减少手动点击和检查等重复性工作，从而节省时间，提升工作效率。

data.title: Show HN: Heart Rate Zones Plus – The first iOS app I developed
data.author: tobias5
data.article_summary: Heart Rate Zones Plus是一款专注于心率区间分析的健身追踪应用，帮助用户了解和监控自己在不同心率区间的时间分配，从而更有效地达成健身目标。主要功能包括自定义时间段追踪、具体锻炼对心率区间的贡献分析、多种心率区间计算方法、个性化目标设置以及详细的锻炼数据展示。应用支持黑暗和明亮模式，并注重用户隐私，所有健康数据保留在设备上，不会被存储或共享。该应用适合各类通过心率区间训练的用户，如跑步者、游泳者等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新推出的健身相关应用的用户体验和功能改进建议

不同观点：
• **beingfit**：对无数据追踪功能表示赞赏，但对设置菜单中的一些选项感到困惑。具体包括："Time Period"的最大值为何只有30天、如何选择"Resting Heart Rate"、以及"Metrics and Goals"中的时间段和目标设置不明确。建议增加新手引导和解释文字。
• **swalling**：指出底部工具栏遮挡了Zone 1的测量数据，且无法导入过去的健康数据。建议重新设计信息架构，将不常用的设置移至标题区域，让用户可以通过滑动查看不同视图。
• **jayunit**：对应用表示赞赏，但初次启动时未看到数据，需手动批准健康数据共享。建议在初次会话中引导用户进行此操作，并希望看到上周的信息总结。

• **ellisv**：对应用的发布表示祝贺，分享了自己未完成和未发布的类似应用开发经历，并建议增加新手引导、过滤特定锻炼类型和时长、以及增加主屏幕小组件。
• **ashryan**：对应用表示兴奋，并希望通过应用更好地跟踪每周的心率区间。
• **jondishotsky**：建议增加周五的提醒消息，告知用户哪些训练区间不足，并建议接下来的三天重点关注。

• 争议焦点主要集中在设置和目标的不明确性，以及对Apple Watch支持和数据导入功能的疑问。
• 用户普遍希望增加新手引导和解释文字，以帮助理解和设置应用。
• 多个用户提到希望能够查看历史数据（如上周的信息），并对手动数据录入和心率计算方式表示关注。
• 部分用户对应用的简洁性和实用性表示赞赏，但也有用户对信息架构和界面设计提出改进建议。

data.title: Joining Sun Microsystems – 40 years ago (2022)
data.author: TMWNN
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者40年前加入初创公司Sun Microsystems的经历。作者最初在Amdahl Corp工作，负责将UNIX移植到大型机。1980年末，他转至数据通信领域，但并不满意。在参与UNIX和伯克利BSD UNIX工作期间，他结识了Bill Joy等人。1981-1982年，硅谷掀起创业热潮，UNIX和Motorola 68000是热门技术，许多初创公司应运而生。作者通过与多位业内人士交流后，被Sun Microsystems的Scott McNealy邀请面试，并结识了Andy Bechtolsheim和Vinod Khosla。Bill Joy的加入以及UNIX和68000技术的结合促使作者决定加入Sun，成为其第8号员工。作者在Sun的第一年，成功修复了UNIX系统中的磁盘驱动问题，并见证了Sun的快速成长。他对能参与Sun Microsystems的辉煌历程感到无比感激。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对SGI、Sun等科技公司在它们巅峰时期的回顾与反思，以及对Unix和Java发展历程的讨论。

不同观点：
• **JSR_FDED**：回忆在SGI的辉煌时期，强调与聪明同事共事的学习经历以及服务创新型客户的自豪感。然而，市场趋势转向“数钱”的业务（如金融服务），使得原来的技术驱动型市场缩小。
• **gopalv**：通过个人家族历史展示几代人在科技行业中的传承与支持，强调家族网络对职业发展的重要性，并反思现代小家庭结构可能带来的支持缺失问题。
• **jmwilson**：认为在科技公司辉煌时期工作是一种幸运，并以Facebook为例，指出行业有周期性，所有的辉煌都会褪色。
• **otras**：对科技公司兴衰历史的兴趣，寻求推荐关于Sun公司的书籍。
• **ajross**：详细分析Sun公司的快速崛起与衰落，强调其在Unix技术创新中的核心地位，以及后期被Linux和其他低成本方案取代的过程。对Unix的未来发展表示疑惑。

补充讨论：
• **mise_en_place**：赞扬Sun公司员工的才华，并提到从他们身上学到很多，尤其是结对编程时的经验。
• **mrcwinn**：以幽默方式回应JSR_FDED的评论，强调其在那个时代的“酷”元素。
• **LastTrain**：简短评论，讽刺“底部喂食者”（bottom feeders）在家庭酿造市场的失败。
• **jeffrallen**：推荐与Lyons相关的播客，展示对科技社区中人物的关注。
• **berlinbrowndev**：对Java如何从Sun的生态中成长出来表示好奇。
• **minitoar和zkmon**：对图片和Sun被卖给Oracle的决定表示兴趣和疑惑。

争议焦点：
• **Sun的衰落原因**：ajross和JSR_FDED都提到了Sun的辉煌与衰落，讨论了Linux和其他低成本方案对其市场的冲击，以及Java和Oracle在公司后期发展中的角色。
• **家族网络在科技行业中的作用**：gopalv强调家族支持对个人职业发展的重要性，而现代小家庭结构可能削弱了这种支持。

整体来看，评论主要围绕Sun及其他科技公司的历史、技术创新、市场变化及个人职业经历展开。

43846187.article_content:
pugs78
Silicon Valley
,
UNIX
May 3, 2022
May 23, 2022
3 Minutes
40 years ago today:  I joined a tiny startup called Sun Microsystems. What a ride! Here’s the never-before-told story of how I arrived at Sun as employee #8! 🧵
I started out in Silicon Valley in June of 1978 working at Amdahl Corp. porting UNIX to the mainframe, a revival of the work started at Princeton in 1975.
Sometime in late ’80 I moved over to Amdahl’s architecture group to work on data communications – X.25, SNA, etc.  But that work wasn’t too satisfying.
During the UNIX/UTS work I had been up to Berkeley a few times to see talks by Bill Joy and others about BSD UNIX (I think I was the first person to implement the select system call, though it never made it to product). Anyways, I guess Bill remembered me.
There was *intense* startup fever in the Silicon Valley in 81/82. I  was caught up in it and actively looking for a startup – I even bought books and magazines about starting companies.
🔥🔥🔥 At that time UNIX and Motorola 68000 were HOT technologies 🔥🔥🔥 – there were literally (yes, truly) 100 startup companies doing something with the combination.
Most of the well-funded ones were building time-shared minicomputers to attack DEC – Altos Computer Systems was a prime example. There were a bunch of bottom feeders targeting the home-brew market, and then there were a few with real differentiation.
I had talked with Valid Logic Systems, who were building a CAD workstation. Good people, but CAD was not my thing so I didn’t have any feeling about the business.
I also talked with Fortune Systems. John Bass, pretty well known in the UNIX world, was there and trying to get me. Fortune was very well funded and going after the Wang word processing market. I still have never seen a Wang system in person, so that was not my bag either.
But let’s talk about my unfair advantage – my Lyon family mafia. I was living with my brother Bob and his wife. Bob was working at Xerox SDD developing the Xerox Star workstation. And my brother Dick was at Xerox PARC with an Alto on his desk! So I knew workstations.
Bob had a friend from SDD, Glenn, who would come over to our house to shoot the breeze; and he started raving one time about the SUN project at Stanford and about how cool the processor board was, and how we should all buy one if we could (for homebrew hacking).
So I knew about SUN. One day Scott McNealy called me out of the blue, having found me at Amdahl. He said he was with a company called Sun Microsystems. I responded “Oh! Are you doing something with the SUN board?”  He was NOT expecting that.
So I went for an interview and met Scott, Andy Bechtolsheim, and Vinod Khosla. That’s when they told me that they had landed Bill Joy – and that was who gave Scott my name (on a list with 20+ others). The combination of UNIX, workstations, and Bill Joy sealed the deal for me.
My bit of diligence was to check with my brother Dick about Andy B.  Andy had interned with Xerox PARC while developing the SUN 3Mb Ethernet card. Dick assured me he had a good reputation.
So I got an offer letter from Vinod. When talking to him about it, I pushed a little on the stock option number. He reacted viscerally with “That’s a good number!”  I think others had already moved him to a higher amount. Anyways, I was a push-over. I accepted.
When I told my brother Bob, he was rather distressed. We were just managing a house mortgage with 3 full time incomes. Interest rates then were well above 10%. But no worries; a year later he was at Sun too.
I started on May 3. Bruce Smith, employee #9, started the same day. We each followed the other around for a while thinking they had been there already. The office was at 2310 Walsh in Santa Clara, across from today’s Nvidia campus.
Bill Shannon(RIP) started a couple of weeks later with lots of BSD UNIX experience already, and together we were the fearsome kernel team. His fun title was “virtual memory manager” and mine was “director of devices”
My first success at Sun was in debugging a disk driver in UNISOFT UNIX (a V7 port for the 68K). The bug would scramble the disk whenever swapping started. With the fix, we could ship UNIX with Sun-1s.
A year after I started, Sun was a whole lot of great people with new buildings in Mountain View, shipping zillions of workstations with BSD UNIX, 68010s, and 10Mb Ethernet.
I am eternally grateful for the opportunity to have been part of the Sun Microsystems phenomenon.

data.title: OCaml's Wings for Machine Learning
data.author: musha68k
data.article_summary: Raven是OCaml的一个机器学习生态系统，包含一系列库和工具，旨在为OCaml引入高效的机器学习和数据科学能力。其核心项目包括Ndarray（类似NumPy的高性能数值计算库）、Ndarray-CV（计算机视觉工具）、Ndarray-IO（数据读写库）、Ndarray-Datasets（提供常用数据集）、Quill（交互式笔记本应用）和Hugin（可视化库）。Raven目前处于pre-alpha阶段，正寻求用户反馈，目标是使OCaml在机器学习任务中的使用像Python一样直观，同时保持OCaml的类型安全和性能优势。Raven采用ISC许可证，欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OCaml及其在机器学习中的应用，与其他语言和工具的比较

不同观点：
• [toolslive] 认为不喜欢使用笔记本（notebooks）来编写代码，更偏好如IPython这样的交互式环境，同时使用自己喜欢的代码编辑器，而不是在浏览器中编写代码。他质疑为何不使用REPL（如OCaml的REPL）来获得类似的体验。

• [behnamoh] 对OCaml的表现感到惊讶，虽然OCaml在特性和库方面已经成熟，且有一个小而热情的社区，但他个人更倾向于使用Haskell和Elixir，每次尝试接受OCaml时都会被后两者吸引。

• [deredede] 对OCaml在机器学习领域的新努力表示兴趣，并提到Owl项目（一个较早的OCaml科学计算项目）。他比较了Owl和Raven（新项目），指出Raven更注重开发者体验和无缝集成，而Owl的使用体验相对痛苦，尤其是在与Numpy对比时。

• [FrustratedMonky] 询问是否有人使用FSharp进行类似机器学习和AI的开发，认为FSharp可能拥有比OCaml更完善的生态系统，同时保留了OCaml的功能性。

• [cube2222] 对OCaml在机器学习领域的潜力表示期待，但不太相信OCaml能从Python手中抢到大量用户。他认为OCaml是一门可爱的语言，但遗憾于它的不流行。

• [evacchi] 以幽默的方式评论，认为终于有人把“机器学习”放进“ML”（OCaml的语言名称缩写是ML），暗示OCaml在机器学习领域的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是OCaml与Haskell、Elixir等语言的比较，以及其在机器学习领域的实际应用体验。
• 另一个讨论点是OCaml与FSharp的比较，以及FSharp在机器学习生态系统中的潜在优势。
• 对OCaml在机器学习领域的未来发展潜力表示期待，但对其能否与Python竞争持怀疑态度。
• 对Owl和Raven这两个OCaml项目的比较，以及开发者体验的讨论。

Raven
OCaml's Wings for Machine Learning
Raven is a comprehensive ecosystem of libraries, frameworks, and tools that brings machine learning and data science capabilities to OCaml.
Vision
Raven aims to make training models, running data science tasks, and building pipelines in OCaml as efficient and intuitive as Python, while leveraging OCaml's inherent type safety and performance advantages. We prioritize developer experience and seamless integration.
Status
Raven is currently in
pre-alpha
and we're seeking user feedback:
Ndarray
and
Hugin
: Scope is feature-complete for the first alpha release, though feedback may influence refinements.
Rune
: Proof-of-concept stage.
Quill
: Early prototyping phase.
The Ecosystem
Raven is a constellation of sub-projects, each addressing a specific aspect of the machine learning and data science workflow:
Ndarray
: The core of Raven, providing high-performance numerical computation with multi-device support (CPU, GPU), similar to NumPy but with OCaml's type safety.
Ndarray-CV
: A collection of computer vision utilities built on top of Ndarray.
Ndarray-IO
: A library for reading and writing Ndarray data in various formats.
Ndarray-Datasets
: Easy access to popular machine learning and data.
science datasets as Ndarrays.
Quill
: An interactive notebook application for data exploration, prototyping, and knowledge sharing.
Hugin
: A visualization library that produces publication-quality plots and charts.
Rune
: A library for automatic differentiation and JIT compilation, inspired by JAX.
(More to come!)
: Raven is an evolving ecosystem, and we have exciting plans for additional libraries and tools to make OCaml a premier choice for machine learning and data science.
Python vs Raven: A Comparison
The table below compares Python's popular data science libraries with their Raven counterparts. For detailed code examples, see the linked documentation files.

data.title: Retailers will soon have only about 7 weeks of full inventories left
data.author: andrewfromx
data.article_summary: 据港口执行董事Gene Seroka警告，在美国与中国之间的贸易战背景下，洛杉矶港的零售商库存即将仅剩约7周的完整库存。由于持续的关税和贸易紧张，进口商正面临供应链中断和成本上升的问题。Seroka指出，尽管港口努力提高效率，但持续的贸易争端可能导致商品短缺和价格上涨，影响美国消费者。这一情况凸显了贸易战对全球供应链的深远影响，并可能加剧经济不确定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国对华关税政策及其潜在经济影响

不同观点：
• **短期痛苦，长期收益？**  
  - **toddmorey** 提出，政治上关税政策被视为短期痛苦、长期收益，但他找不到经济学家支持这一理论。仅少数如Jeff Ferry认为历史上的关税政策促进了美国工业化，但当前全球供应链的现实不同。
  
• **供应链危机的严重性**  
  - **faefox** 强调，一旦现有库存耗尽，供应链问题将比COVID期间的冲击更严重，且这次是“自我造成”的，可能无法恢复。

• **地缘政治策略**  
  - **mediumsmart** 认为，关税政策可能是为了通过孤立中国来施压，并期待在7周内看到结果。但他对美国经济是否受益持怀疑态度。

• **社会和经济混乱**  
  - **fudged71** 和 **inverted_flag** 提到了可能的商品短缺和抢购潮，类似于之前的厕纸恐慌。
  - **mindcrash** 警告，如果关税政策持续，可能会影响整个西方经济，而不仅是美国。

• **非传统解决方案和犯罪组织参与**  
  - **MaoSYJ** 提出，贩毒集团可能会利用其走私基础设施来解决物流问题，暗示犯罪组织可能参与走私高价值产品。

• **消费者行为和反资本主义观点**  
  - **deadbabe** 认为反资本主义者可能会支持关税政策，因为减少消费和商业激励符合其理念。

• **历史对比与当前危机**  
  - **cynicalsecurity** 将美国当前的商品短缺与苏联时期做对比，警告如果持续，可能会重蹈覆辙。

• **全球视角**  
  - **foobar1962** 指出，只有美国零售商受到影响，其他国家则观望事态发展，类似于看戏吃爆米花。

补充讨论：
• **当前影响已经显现**  
  - **alchemist1e9** 观察到，大零售商已经出现大量商品短缺。

• **美国中心视角**  
  - **k4rli** 强调，讨论中提到零售商时应明确是美国零售商。

争议焦点：
• **关税政策是否能带来长期经济收益**  
  一方认为关税可能促进美国工业化，另一方则认为当前全球化背景下，供应链中断带来的风险远大于收益。

• **供应链危机的严重性和可恢复性**  
  部分评论认为供应链危机会非常严重且可能不可恢复，另一方则持相对乐观态度，认为短期波动后会恢复正常。

data.article_summary: 美国洛杉矶港执行董事Gene Seroka表示，由于特朗普政府对华加征关税，美国从中国的货物运输量将大幅下降。预计下周抵达西海岸的货物量将比去年同期减少超过三分之一，降幅约35%。洛杉矶港约45%的业务来自中国，但许多美国零售商已停止从中国发货。一些运输公司试图从东南亚其他地区补货，但整体贸易量仍将显著减少。此外，五到七周后，美国零售商库存将开始受到影响，可能导致商品选择减少和价格上涨。经济学家警告，进口减少可能引发美国运输和零售行业裁员，甚至导致经济衰退。

不同观点：
• **对港口数据的关注**：dten提到洛杉矶港有免费的实时数据面板，并指出某些周的货运量同比下降35%，但随后一周预测会有25%的增长。该评论侧重于数据分析和趋势预测。

• **国际运输成本上升**：mstaoru提到从中国到欧盟的国际搬运费用比三个月前高了2.5-3倍，海运检查更严格，空运因运量低而更贵，表明当前国际运输面临挑战。

• **潜在的经济影响**：taylodl担心物流问题可能导致商品短缺，甚至比疫情初期的厕纸抢购更严重。dr_pardee则指出，有人通过规避关税的方式减少影响，并分享了一些相关链接。

• **供应链和仓储的连锁反应**：guywithahat提到洛杉矶经济很大程度上依赖仓库，这可能影响住房成本，进而影响菲尼克斯等其他地区。pelagic_sky指出西雅图港口目前是空的，并提供了一篇文章链接。

• **零售商的应对策略**：duxup提出零售商可能会选择提高价格或干脆不提供某些商品，以应对供应链问题。

• **更广泛的贸易影响**：rtkwe担心全面的关税政策可能导致船只因不满载而不来美国，影响其他东南亚贸易。

Key Points
"It's a precipitous drop in volume with a number of major American retailers stopping all shipments from China based on the tariffs," said Gene Seroka, executive director of the Port of Los Angeles.
Shipments from China make up about 45% of the business for the port, though some transport companies will be looking to pick up goods at other points in Southeast Asia to try to fill up their ships, Seroka said.
Data on shipments out of China had already started to signal slowing trade volume to the U.S., alarming some economists.
A container ship is shown at the Port of Los Angeles in Los Angeles, California, U.S. November 22, 2021.
Mike Blake | Reuters
Shipments from China to the West Coast of the U.S. will plummet next week as the impact of President
Donald Trump
's tariffs leads companies to cut their import orders.
Gene Seroka, executive director of the Port of Los Angeles, said Tuesday on
CNBC's "Squawk Box
" that he expects incoming cargo volume to slide by more than a third next week compared with the same period in 2024.
"According to our own port optimizer, which measures the loadings in Asia, we'll be down just a little bit over 35% next week compared to last year. And it's a precipitous drop in volume with a number of major American retailers stopping all shipments from China based on the tariffs," Seroka said.
watch now
VIDEO
6:04
06:04
Port of LA's Gene Seroka on tariff impact: Retailers have about 5-7 weeks of full inventories left
Squawk Box
Shipments from China make up about 45% of the business for the Port of LA, though some transport companies will be looking to pick up goods at other points in Southeast Asia to try to fill up their ships, Seroka said.
"Realistically speaking, until some accord or framework can be reached with China, the volume coming out of there — save a couple of different commodities — will be very light at best," Seroka said.
Along with the lower volume of goods, Seroka said he expects roughly a quarter of the usual number of arriving ships to the port to be canceled in May.
Trump announced a sharp increase in tariffs on Chinese goods on April 2, which led to escalation on both sides, eventually resulting in both the U.S. and China imposing levies of more than 100% on many goods from each other. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has described the situation as "unsustainable" but there has been no sign of substantial negotiations between the two countries.
Data on shipments out of China had already started to
signal slowing trade volume
to the U.S., alarming some economists. Apollo Global Management's chief economist, Torsten Slok, recently laid out a timeline where lower imports from China leads to layoffs in transportation and retail industries in the U.S., empty shelves and a
recession this summer
.
Seroka said he thinks U.S. retailers have about five to seven weeks before the impact of the curtailed shipments begins to bite, partly because companies stocked up ahead of Trump's tariff announcements.
"I don't see a complete emptiness on store shelves or online when we're buying. But if you're out looking for a blue shirt, you might find 11 purple ones and one blue in a size that's not yours. So we'll start seeing less choice on those shelves simply because we're not getting the variety of goods coming in here based on the additional costs in place. And for that one blue shirt that's still left, you'll see a price hike," Seroka said.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某安全工具的评价与反馈，涵盖营销表述、技术功能、用户体验及工具比较等方面。

不同观点：
• [ziddoap] 对营销文案中"保证安全性"的表述提出质疑，认为没有任何工具能完全保证云环境的安全，这种表述容易让人联想到不靠谱的VPN公司。虽然对产品本身未有深入评价，但此类表述影响其对产品的信任。
• [jmpavlec] 指出GitHub描述中存在多个错别字，具体在描述语句中，如"monitoring"被写成"monitoring and manage alerting"等，可能会影响专业形象。
• [stego-tech] 对工具的自动化合规和漏洞管理功能表示期待，但也反馈了在iPhone 14 Pro上的显示问题，如文本不换行、图形不缩放、列不对齐等。
• [mrbluecoat] 对工具的Logo设计提出主观看法，调侃其像老鼠或 optical illusion 图片，但同时也对工具提升公司安全态势的努力表示赞赏。
• [sontek] 询问该工具的政策引擎相对于Cloud Custodian的优势，寻求更详细的解释。
• [zufallsheld] 关心该工具是否可以在不依赖SaaS组件的情况下运行，尤其是在隔离网络环境中（air-gapped）。
• [gitroom] 对工具简化安全管理表示赞赏，个人非常感兴趣。
• [shooker435] 询问该工具是否可以替代或补充类似Vanta的工具，关心其功能重叠与互补性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于营销文案中的"安全性保证"表述，[ziddoap]认为这种说法不严谨且容易引起误解，影响用户信任。
• 用户对工具的功能表示期待，但也提出了一些技术细节上的问题，如是否支持离线运行、政策引擎的优势等。
• 用户体验问题集中在移动端显示问题，如[stego-tech]反馈的iPhone显示异常，这可能影响产品的用户体验。

data.title: No as a Service
data.author: radeeyate
data.article_summary:
No-as-a-Service (NAAS) 是一个简单的 API，提供随机的拒绝理由，适合用于需要合理或有趣的拒绝场景。它可以用于个人、工作、学生生活等各种场合，提供礼貌或机智的“不”。API 基本信息如下：

- **URL**: https://naas.isalman.dev/no
- **Method**: GET
- **Rate Limit**: 每分钟每个IP地址最多10次请求

例如：
```json
{
  "reason": "This feels like something Future Me would yell at Present Me for agreeing to."
}
```

用户也可以自行部署：
1. 克隆仓库并安装依赖
2. 启动服务器，默认端口3000，可自定义。

项目结构简单，主要包括一个 Express API 和一个包含 1000 多条拒绝理由的 JSON 文件。该项目基于 MIT 许可。

作者是 hotheadhacker，项目在 GitHub 获得 337 个星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个API服务的实现、重复响应消息的原因、技术优化建议及幽默评论

不同观点：
• [varun_ch, seabass] 提到了API返回了"请求过多"的错误信息，seabass特别指出这是一个错过幽默的机会。
• [deanputney, ziddoap] 发现`reasons.json`文件中存在大量重复的响应，如某条消息重复了45次。他们质疑这种重复是否是为了处理某种分布问题。
• [hombre_fatal] 从个人经验出发，认为这种简单的项目在技术成熟后可能会被视为不值得单独作为一个项目存在，甚至可能会被删除。
• [anonymousiam] 指出在1000个可能的响应中，实际上只有26个是独特的，暗示项目的潜力有限。
• [choult] 提到该服务是基于一个近期的网络迷因（meme）创建的，暗示其流行性。
• [n8m8] 幽默地预测有人会不理解为什么不用LLM（大型语言模型）来实现这个服务。

补充讨论：
• [Retr0id] 提出该服务若要更有用，可以增加各种HTTP失败模式，如不同的HTTP状态码、TLS证书问题、超时、重定向循环等，从而用于测试HTTP客户端。
• [qrush] 以幽默的方式将该服务比作"Balatro的命运之轮卡片作为服务"（Balatro是桌游中一个以随机性著称的角色）。
• [Haeuserschlucht, artogahr] 仅以微笑符号回应，表示对讨论内容的轻松态度。
• [blahaj] 关注API的速率限制，认为每分钟10次的限制过于严格，并质疑该限制是否针对Cloudflare反向代理而非原始IP地址。

争议焦点：
- 重复响应消息的合理性：部分用户质疑为何响应消息需要重复多达50次，猜测可能是为了处理分布问题，但没有确凿解释。
- API速率限制的合理性：blahaj认为每分钟10次的请求限制过于严格，尤其是在该服务看似资源消耗很低的情况下，并对速率限制的实施方式提出质疑。

总体来看，讨论围绕项目的技术实现、实用性及幽默性展开，部分参与者提供了技术改进建议，而其他人则以幽默或个人经验回应。

❌ No-as-a-Service
Ever needed a graceful way to say “no”?
This tiny API returns random, generic, creative, and sometimes hilarious rejection reasons — perfectly suited for any scenario: personal, professional, student life, dev life, or just because.
Built for humans, excuses, and humor.
🚀 API Usage
Base URL
https://naas.isalman.dev/no
Method:
GET
Rate Limit:
10 requests per minute per IP
🔄 Example Request
GET
/no
✅ Example Response
{
"reason"
:
"
This feels like something Future Me would yell at Present Me for agreeing to.
"
}
Use it in apps, bots, landing pages, Slack integrations, rejection letters, or wherever you need a polite (or witty) no.
🛠️ Self-Hosting
Want to run it yourself? It’s lightweight and simple.
1. Clone this repository
git clone https://github.com/hotheadhacker/no-as-a-service.git
cd
no-as-a-service
2. Install dependencies
npm install
3. Start the server
npm start
The API will be live at:
http://localhost:3000/no
You can also change the port using an environment variable:
PORT=5000 npm start

├── index.js            # Express API

43845016.article_summary:
No-as-a-Service (NAAS) 是一个简单的 API，提供随机的拒绝理由，适合用于需要合理或有趣的拒绝场景。它可以用于个人、工作、学生生活等各种场合，提供礼貌或机智的“不”。API 基本信息如下：

- **URL**: https://naas.isalman.dev/no
- **Method**: GET
- **Rate Limit**: 每分钟每个IP地址最多10次请求

例如：
```json
{
  "reason": "This feels like something Future Me would yell at Present Me for agreeing to."
}
```

用户也可以自行部署：
1. 克隆仓库并安装依赖
2. 启动服务器，默认端口3000，可自定义。

项目结构简单，主要包括一个 Express API 和一个包含 1000 多条拒绝理由的 JSON 文件。该项目基于 MIT 许可。

作者是 hotheadhacker，项目在 GitHub 获得 337 个星标。
43845016.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个API服务的实现、重复响应消息的原因、技术优化建议及幽默评论

不同观点：
• [varun_ch, seabass] 提到了API返回了"请求过多"的错误信息，seabass特别指出这是一个错过幽默的机会。
• [deanputney, ziddoap] 发现`reasons.json`文件中存在大量重复的响应，如某条消息重复了45次。他们质疑这种重复是否是为了处理某种分布问题。
• [hombre_fatal] 从个人经验出发，认为这种简单的项目在技术成熟后可能会被视为不值得单独作为一个项目存在，甚至可能会被删除。
• [anonymousiam] 指出在1000个可能的响应中，实际上只有26个是独特的，暗示项目的潜力有限。
• [choult] 提到该服务是基于一个近期的网络迷因（meme）创建的，暗示其流行性。
• [n8m8] 幽默地预测有人会不理解为什么不用LLM（大型语言模型）来实现这个服务。

补充讨论：
• [Retr0id] 提出该服务若要更有用，可以增加各种HTTP失败模式，如不同的HTTP状态码、TLS证书问题、超时、重定向循环等，从而用于测试HTTP客户端。
• [qrush] 以幽默的方式将该服务比作"Balatro的命运之轮卡片作为服务"（Balatro是桌游中一个以随机性著称的角色）。
• [Haeuserschlucht, artogahr] 仅以微笑符号回应，表示对讨论内容的轻松态度。
• [blahaj] 关注API的速率限制，认为每分钟10次的限制过于严格，并质疑该限制是否针对Cloudflare反向代理而非原始IP地址。

争议焦点：
- 重复响应消息的合理性：部分用户质疑为何响应消息需要重复多达50次，猜测可能是为了处理分布问题，但没有确凿解释。
- API速率限制的合理性：blahaj认为每分钟10次的请求限制过于严格，尤其是在该服务看似资源消耗很低的情况下，并对速率限制的实施方式提出质疑。

总体来看，讨论围绕项目的技术实现、实用性及幽默性展开，部分参与者提供了技术改进建议，而其他人则以幽默或个人经验回应。

43837751.article_content:
I've had my own website practically forever. Back in the late '90s, I already had a web page on my ISP's server, and since at least 2001, I've had my own homepage on my own server. I've never been a great graphic designer, let alone a skilled webmaster, so I've always tried to keep things minimal and compatible.
Initially, like many others, I wrote HTML pages by hand. Then I used WYSIWYG creation tools, and eventually, I landed on CMS (Content Management Systems).
The Era of Dynamic CMS
I liked
CMS
because they allowed me to focus on the content and not on the correctness of the generated HTML. Thanks to them, I started writing my first blog shortly afterward.
Over the years, I've used many tools like PHPNuke, FlatNuke (created and developed by my friend
Simone Vellei
), eventually moving through Joomla and Wordpress. Wordpress always seemed like the most suitable tool for the job, and I used it for many years. Even today, mainly on the sysadmin side, I manage hundreds of Wordpress sites, and they are reasonably reliable, aside from the plugins (because
the problem with Wordpress isn't the software itself, but many of the external plugins
).
But this is precisely the problem: all dynamic CMS require constant and continuous security updates because, without them, the chances of defacement are extremely high.
Discovering Static Site Generators
And that's precisely why, when I discovered Carlos Fenollosa's
bashblog
in 2014, it immediately became clear that, indeed, there was no reason to continue down the path of dynamic CMS. I don't write often, I don't update often, there's no reason to regenerate all the content with every visit. Sure, WordPress caching plugins are often quite effective, but they are still add-ons that need to be kept up to date. And I'm not a fan of adding things to streamline. Often, less is more.
So, I started using bashblog for some 'secondary' projects until, in 2015, I
migrated my 'old' Italian blog from WordPress to Pelican
. Shortly after, I
moved from Pelican to Nikola
, and that blog is still generated by Nikola, although (that blog's) updates are now extremely rare (so much so that I consider it almost abandoned). I also created the first Docker container for Nikola and, for a long time, it was listed among the deployment methods on their site.
Building My Own: BSSG
But bashblog continued to fascinate me. So in 2015, for fun, I started developing my own Static Site Generator from scratch. I called it (with little imagination),
BSSG - Bash Static Site Generator
. The plan was for it to be compatible with the main OSes I use, to remain sufficiently simple and straightforward (!!!), and to be tailored to my needs. I intended to use it only and exclusively for small private things, starting with a sort of diary of mine - more professional than personal - and leave the 'official' blogs to more tested and 'professional' tools.
As time went by, I added some small features I liked: theming support, archives, tags (initially absent). Over time, many functions were added, and the script grew large â large enough to make me pause and ask myself some questions about the long-term stability of this solution. So, it remained only for my 'diary', which, however, grew year after year to the point where I needed to devise some kind of optimization. I then developed (more for fun than out of real necessity) a caching system. On rebuild, only what needs to be rebuilt is reconstructed, making the operation sufficiently fast even as the number of posts grows. Obviously, there are limits: using bash and external tools, the efficiency cannot be compared to that of a proper programming language.
Brief Detour: ITNBlog
And it's here that I decided, in preparation for opening a new blog (this one), to create a new tool called
ITNBlog
. I would develop it in Python and focus a bit more on performance and completeness. But ITNBlog stalled very quickly: time was limited, I'm not a full-time developer, so I realized I would spend too much time on development and too little on content creation.
Therefore, in 2018, I launched this blog but using
Ghost
, a solution that gave me good results, including performance-wise. I chose Ghost because I thought that, writing content also from my phone while on the go, a real CMS would be useful. Spoiler: no, it didn't turn out that way, so a few years later I decided to migrate this blog to
Hugo
. Nevertheless, I continued to develop ITNBlog on and off, as a hobby, without any particular ambitions.
At some point, however, I found myself in a particular situation: Hugo deprecated some features, and the theme I had chosen moved forward. But I ended up in an unpleasant situation: using the latest version of Hugo and the current version of the theme would produce unacceptable output; staying with the old version of Hugo while waiting for the theme update meant making a compromise. data.title: Study finds that budget cuts to public R&D would significantly hurt the economy
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 本文简要分析了削减联邦科研经费对宏观经济的负面影响。主要发现包括：削减公共研发经费将长期损害经济，显著降低GDP、投资和政府收入。例如，削减25%的公共研发开支将使GDP下降幅度达到大衰退时期的水平；若削减一半，美国人平均将比历史趋势下预计的少10,000美元收入。此外，削减研发经费还会减少政府收入，25%的削减将使年收入减少4.3%，50%的削减则减少8.6%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国政治中的党派政策及其影响，特别是对红州和科研领域的影响。

不同观点：
• Herring认为投票给共和党会导致红州政策的实施，并指出红州长期以来表现不佳，但选民依然支持共和党。他还提到特朗普赢得了普选，暗示美国正趋向于成为一个大的红州。

• luotuoshangdui简单表示对上述观点的认同，认为这是预料之中的事情。

• minecraft001则用讽刺的语气评论官僚主义，暗示官僚机构自我标榜其重要性，可能质疑其在政策制定中的实际价值。

• readthenotes1关注科研与预算削减的影响，特别是对复制危机（replication crisis）的潜在影响。他提到科研经费削减可能带来的问题，并引用了一篇《自然》杂志的文章来支持其观点。

补充讨论：
• Herring的评论中提到了特朗普的普选胜利，这是一个有争议的观点，因为事实上特朗普在2016年美国总统选举中并未赢得普选，但Herring可能在表达对选举制度的不满。

• readthenotes1引用的文章链接讨论了预算削减对科研的影响，特别是对科学研究真实性和透明度的影响，这是对科研资金削减的深层次担忧。

争议的焦点：
• 共和党和红州政策的效果及其对美国整体的影响是讨论的核心争议点。Herring批评红州政策表现不佳，但依然获得选民支持，而其他评论者未直接反驳这一观点，但minecraft001对官僚机构的讽刺可能隐含对Herring观点的质疑。

• 科研预算削减及其对复制危机的影响是另一个值得关注的争议点，readthenotes1担心这会影响科研的真实性和透明度。

43845695.article_content:
Federal agencies such as NIH and NSF are critical sources of funding for basic and applied scientific research. Recently, many of these agencies have seen their research operations frozen or downsized. This
brief
describes a new analysis of the macroeconomic costs of cutting federal funding for scientific R&D. The brief finds that budget cuts to public R&D would significantly hurt the economy in the long run, with large negative effects on GDP, investment, and government revenue. A 25 percent cut to public R&D spending would reduce GDP by an amount comparable to the decline in GDP during the Great Recession. Cutting annual public R&D spending in half would making the average American approximately $10,000 poorer (in today’s dollars) than the value implied by the historical trend in GDP. Cutting public R&D would also shrink federal government revenue. A 25 percent cut in R&D would decrease revenue by approximately 4.3 percent annually, while a 50 percent cut would decrease it by 8.6 percent annually.

data.title: Lessons from the Lebanese Space Program – Kasurian
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《黎巴嫩太空计划的启示》一文回顾了黎巴嫩火箭学会在冷战时期从无到有创建太空计划的历程。在创始人Manoug Manougian的领导下，这个由Haigazian学院学生和教授组成的小团队，凭借有限的资源和无私的奉献，成功将火箭送入太空。学会初期仅依靠少量捐助和自制材料进行试验，于1961年首次实现火箭升空，并获得总统支持和国家认可。然而，由于地缘政治紧张和战争威胁，加之Manougian对技术军事化的担忧，该项目在1967年被迫中止。黎巴嫩火箭学会的成功展示了创新精神和领导力的重要性，尽管最终未能持续，但它在短暂的时间内为黎巴嫩带来了显著的科学成就和民族自豪感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于黎巴嫩火箭计划的历史及其相关问题

不同观点：
• IG_Semmelweiss认为，Cedar-8火箭几乎击中地中海的一艘英国海军巡洋舰，表明当时黎巴嫩可能没有能力预测火箭降落地点，或者无法与国家行为体沟通危险区域。他还强调，无论资金来源是风投资本还是政府，所有项目都需要进行尽职调查。
• shayway对黎巴嫩在1963年就将火箭送入轨道表示惊讶，并认为这使得黎巴嫩成为世界上第三个实现这一壮举的国家，排在苏联和美国之后。他对自己之前未曾听说过这一历史表示意外，并表示会关注相关纪录片《The Lebanese Rocket Society》。

补充讨论：
• shayway对文章的写作风格提出批评，认为其信息量不足且内容空洞。
• shayway对文章中提到的西方势力介入终止黎巴嫩火箭实验的事件（Cedar-10火箭）表示好奇，希望了解更多背景信息。

争议焦点：
• 关于黎巴嫩火箭计划的安全性和尽职调查问题，IG_Semmelweiss提出质疑，而这一问题在讨论中并未得到完全解答。
• shayway对文章内容的信息量和深度不满，反映出对历史事件的更多细节和背景的需求。

这一讨论揭示了对黎巴嫩早期太空探索和火箭计划的历史认知差异，以及对相关信息和叙述深度的不同期望。

Modest Beginnings
At the height of the Cold War, only a handful of nations possessed the capacity to launch rockets into space. Among them were the world's foremost superpowers of the time: the United States of America (USA), and Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR). Then there was Lebanon, a newly formed Mediterranean nation barely larger than the state of Delaware.
Between 1960 and 1967, the almost forgotten Lebanese Rocket Society, led by its founder Manoug Manougian, competed with the great powers of the Cold War to create a space program in Lebanon. Founded as a student association within the Haigazian College in Beirut in November 1960, the Rocket Society operated without any official funding from the state or the university. Relying on the dedication of a few professors, seven students, and a modest donation from the Lebanese entrepreneur and Parliamentarian Emile Bustani, what the burgeoning Society lacked in resources, it made up for in ingenuity, drive, and vision.
Aiming to elevate Lebanon and the Arab world to the level of the era’s great powers, then locked in a fierce space race, the Rocket Society was an ambitious scientific endeavour. The Rocket Society emerged amid a complex backdrop: Lebanon’s nascent state-building effort, the ebb and flow of Nasserite-coloured Pan-Arabism, ongoing hostilities with Israel, the intensifying Cold War between the USA and USSR, and the yet-unrestricted optimism in technology and its capacity to transform society for the better. This was the now forgotten post-imperial, post-war world of possibility in which the Rocket Society found itself.
Within a few years of its founding, the Rocket Society successfully launched rockets beyond Earth’s atmosphere into space and became a source of national pride for Lebanon. Yet by 1967, it had all but been abandoned by Manougian and much of his team. Escalating geopolitical tensions, diplomatic pressure, war, and Manougian’s fear of the militarisation of his technology would end Lebanon’s brief but remarkable emergence as a space power.
The Rocket Society’s initial success relied not on vast material resources or institutional support but on the singular vision and leadership of Manougian. Born in 1935 in Jericho, Palestine, to a family of Armenian refugees, Manougian was raised and educated in Jerusalem, and in 1955 received a scholarship to study mathematics at the University of Texas, Austin. During his time in Texas, Manougian witnessed the rise of the space race between the USA and USSR. Seized with ambition, and believing that the promise of technology could transform both Lebanon and the Arab world, he planned to put Lebanon on the map. In 1960, at just 25 years old, he returned to Beirut to teach mathematics and physics at the Haigazian College. There, he took charge of the Haigazian Science Club, looking to inspire a new generation of young Lebanese scientists.
What Manougian lacked in formal experience or technical backing, he made up for in his ability to inspire and organise these resourceful students, who required a catalysing force to structure their efforts towards a shared goal. And if there was a space race, why not focus their efforts on rockets? So, the Science Club was renamed the Haigazian College Rocket Society.
The Rocket Society pose in front of a Cedar rocket.
Small Steps and Large Leaps
In the beginning, with few resources at its disposal, everything the Rocket Society built was manufactured locally: prototypes were built using wood, cardboard, metal pipes, and homemade chemical compounds, all produced on-site. The initial tests were conducted without prior trials, often in the gardens of society members' homes in the Lebanese countryside. Nevertheless, in April 1961, they made a breakthrough: a single-stage rocket successfully reached an altitude of two kilometres, a small leap that confirmed they were on the right track. The achievement inspired the team to consider sending an animal, perhaps a mouse, into space. Manougian’s wife shot down that plan.
The success of these initial tests drew the attention of Lebanese President Fouad Chehab, who, in 1961, allocated a budget of 10,000 Lebanese pounds to the project, followed by an additional 15,000 pounds in 1962. The state’s support significantly enhanced the program's capabilities, particularly through the technical and financial assistance of the Lebanese Army. From that point onwards, the rockets were launched from the military base of Dbayeh near Beirut. data.title: U.S. Economy Contracts at 0.3% Rate in First Quarter
data.author: bko
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对当前经济形势和贸易战影响的分析与预测

不同观点：
• [this_user] 认为，经济不喜欢不确定性，在贸易战局势明朗之前，很难做出前瞻性规划。局势拖延越久，对实体经济的损害就越大。
• [jqpabc123] 对政府处理经济数据的手法持讽刺态度，暗示政府通过更换数据编制人员来操控经济信息。
• [lvl155] 批评当前政府政策，认为其破坏了美联储通过降息应对通胀的时机，仿佛有意破坏美国经济。
• [gymbeaux] 以幽默方式引用电影台词，暗示经济可能面临重大牺牲。
• [ty6853] 认为尽管经济可能出现问题，但住房价格不会下降，因为大部分贷款利率极低，房主不会轻易放弃。

补充讨论：
• [os2warpman] 认为经济收缩才刚刚开始，真正的经济紧缩还在后面。
• [zdragnar] 指出当前经济信号混乱，CPI、通胀、就业数据与GDP收缩不一致，让人难以判断真实经济状况。
• [dsign] 以外部视角将美国经济问题比作泰坦尼克号沉没，并提到其他国家对美国经济困境的旁观态度，同时表达了对美国民众的同情。
• [celsoazevedo] 猜测在关税正式生效前，许多人提前购买商品以规避涨价，这可能对未来经济数据有影响。
• [isitsafeyet] 提到其投资顾问对当前政策的担忧，并预测如果关税不解除，投资组合策略将大幅改变。
• [acdha] 引用亚特兰大联储的预测数据，认为经济下滑才刚开始，未来可能更加严重。
• [fabian2k] 分享了特朗普在Truth Social上的言论，特朗普将经济问题归咎于拜登，并呼吁耐心等待经济繁荣。fabian2k对此持怀疑态度，认为经济现实难以被否认。
• [jmull] 认为经济形势会进一步恶化，当前数据只是暂时的，关税的真正影响还未显现，经济下滑才刚开始。

争议焦点：
• 当前经济问题的责任归属，部分评论批评特朗普或拜登政府的政策失误。
• 对未来经济走势的判断，一部分人认为经济会进一步恶化，另一部分人则对官方数据和政府说法持怀疑态度。

data.title: "AI-first" is the new Return To Office
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了科技公司CEO们近期热衷于推行“AI优先”策略的现象。作者认为，这种策略可能暗示公司不信任员工的能力，因为AI工具主要对不擅长某项工作的人有帮助，而对于专家来说并非最佳选择。文章以Shopify和Duolingo的CEO为例，指出他们要求员工在绩效考核中体现AI使用情况，这种做法并不寻常。作者认为，CEO们推行AI优先更多是出于群体思维和炫耀心态，而非实际需求。文章建议，公司应根据实际需求合理评估和部署AI工具，而不是强制推行。这种“AI优先”潮流可能忽视了员工的专业能力，也未充分考虑工具的适用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI技术在企业中自上而下强制推行的讨论，包括对这种推行方式的必要性、效果以及可能的负面影响的分析。

不同观点：
• [hbsbsbsndk] 认为Shopify的CEO Tobi像是一个模仿Elon Musk的人，过度关注个人形象，并且通过"跳过招聘队列"等噱头来吸引眼球。评论质疑这种"表演型CEO"的行为，并举例说明公司内部文化可能存在问题。

• [JimDabell] 和 [flappyeagle] 支持自上而下推行新技术，认为历史上很多重要的技术革新（如电子表格、版本控制等）最初都遭遇了抵制，但最终通过强制推行得以普及。他们认为AI技术也有类似情况，初期抵制是正常的，推行的目的是为了克服员工的惯性。

• [andy99] 和 [lsy] 持反对意见，认为强制推行新技术（如AI）往往是管理层在失败前的挣扎，表明该技术可能并不成熟或不适合。他们担心这种推行方式会导致不良的产品开发激励机制，并可能错过更好的技术应用方式。

• [Workaccount2] 提出在非科技行业，AI技术有巨大的潜力，可以帮助非技术人员完成任务，并认为这些行业的CEO可能会积极推动AI的应用。这与其他评论中对科技行业的关注点形成对比。

• [srveale] 部分同意JimDabell的观点，但指出并非所有新技术都需要强制推行，例如电子病历系统的推行虽然遭遇抵制，但最终被广泛接受。评论还提到，强制使用AI可能引发员工的恐慌。

• [resolutefunctor] 批评对CEO和技术推行的过度负面评价，认为强制推行AI是公司领导层的一种战略赌博，可能成功也可能失败。评论还强调AI技术的潜力，认为如果推行得当，可以提高员工的工作效率。

• [hintymad] 对CEO推行AI持理解态度，认为公司领导需要确保不错过重大技术转变，历史上如微软和英特尔的成功转型都是通过自上而下的强制推行实现的。评论认为，即使推行失败，公司也能从中学习。

• [guywithahat] 认为AI可能会取代远程工作员工，因为AI擅长执行狭窄的任务，而员工需要在公司内部建立关系和推动公司发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于自上而下推行AI的必要性和效果。支持者认为这是克服员工惯性的必要手段，反对者则担心这种推行方式会导致不良的产品开发和错过更好的技术应用。
• 不同评论中提到的具体例子（如智能手机、版本控制、电子医疗记录等）为讨论提供了实际支持，并展示了历史上技术推行中的类似情况。
• 对CEO形象和公司文化的讨论也为技术推行的背景提供了更广泛的视角，特别是关于CEO是否在"表演"其技术领导者角色。

43845089.article_content:
The latest fad amongst tech CEOs is no longer "founder mode", or taking drugs that they would fire you for taking, or telling everybody to return to the office — it's demanding that all work be AI-first! This is a great idea if you think nobody at your company is great at what they do. It may otherwise be a suboptimal strategy. Let's dive in!
Let's use me as a case study. I'm pretty okay at writing. For example, one time I
wrote a fairly technical analysis
of Twitter's platform strategy that inspired Will.I.Am of the Black Eyed Peas to start Twitter beef with me two years later when he read the post and took offense to my referring to him as "nobody’s favorite rapper".
This is something your GPTs cannot do, I assure you. An average LLM won't even know that Drake's favorite MIME type is
application/pdf
. Chalk one up for the greatness of human creativity.
The AI-First Mind Virus
Shopify's CEO Tobi Lütke (personal motto: "what if a Canadian was all the worst things about the United States?") started the "AI-first" trend, with
one of those big memos
that included, amongst other things, the declaration that "We will add Al usage questions to our performance and peer review questionnaire." This is unusual — did your boss ever have to send you a memo demanding that you use a smartphone? Was there a performance review requiring you to use Slack? I'm actually old enough that I was at different workplaces when they started using spreadsheets and email and the web, and I can tell you, they absolutely didn't have to drive adoption by making people fill out paperwork about how they were definitely using the cool new technology. Isn't that interesting?
Some of the other CEOs talking about the use of AI are a little more reasonable. Duolingo's CEO Luis von Ahn seems to be trying to be
somewhat
more moderate in
his memo
, stating plainly that he doesn't see AI replacing his employees. (Though that does immediately raise the "who brought that up?" question...) Yet even in this more even-handed take, we still get the insistence that "Al use will be part of what we evaluate in performance reviews". This is really weird!
The funny thing is, I'm not saying LLMs are without their uses. Let's use me as a case study again. I'm a lousy coder, these days. I haven't had time to keep up my skills, and the area I focused on for most of my dev career (front end web development) changes particularly quickly. So I use some of the modern tools to help me get up to speed and get more done in a limited amount of time, because otherwise I'm woefully unproductive in the short windows I have to code in my free time.
To be explicit: I code on the weekends, not professionally. That means I'm not very good at it. I'm certainly
nothing
like the incredibly talented developers that I've had the good fortune to work with over the years. I'm just fluent enough to be able to debug the broken code that LLMs generate, or to catch the bugs that they spew out by default. And I'm sure I don't even catch all the bugs that pop up, but fortunately, I'm not making any production systems; I'm just building little toy apps and sites for myself.
This is an important illustration: AI is really good for helping you if you're bad at something, or at least below average. But it's probably not the right tool if you're great at something. So why would these CEOs be saying, almost all using the exact same phrasing, that everyone at their companies should be using these tools? Do they think their employees are all bad at their jobs?
Groupthink and signaling
Big tech CEOs and VCs really love performing for each other. We know they hang out in group chats like high schoolers, preening and sending each other texts, each trying to make sure they're all wearing the latest fashions, whether it's a gold chain or a MAGA hat or just repeating a phrase that they heard from another founder. A key way of showing that they're part of this cohort is to make sure they're having a tantrum and acting out against their workers fairly regularly.
The return to office fad was a big part of this effort, often largely motivated by reacting to the show of worker power in the racial justice activism efforts of 2020. Similarly, being AI-first shows that a company is participating in the AI trend in the "right" way, by imposing it on workers, rather than trusting workers to judge what tools are useful for them to do their jobs.
A more normal policy on AI at a company might be something like this:
Our IT department has evaluated a set of LLM tools and determined that these ones meet our requirements for security, performance, data governance, reliability, manageability and integration with our workflows. We'll be doing a controlled deployment of these tools and you can choose to use them if you think they'll help you with your work; please share your feedback on whether they are helpful, and what might make them more useful for you over time. Here are the ways these AI tools meet our corporate stand

data.author: royalroad
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了英国树篱在历史、艺术和农业中的角色及其变迁。自1945年以来，约50%的英格兰树篱因农业生产需要被移除，导致生物多样性下降。二战后，为了解决粮食短缺问题，政府推动农业合理化，树篱被视为妨碍生产的存在。1947年农业法案加速了这一进程，虽然有效结束了战后物资匮乏，但也加速了树篱的消失。

然而，树篱并非永久固定，它们随农业需求和经济变化而波动。自公元前2500年以来，农民利用树篱作为农业工具，提供庇护、防风和土地划分。树篱还为多种动植物提供栖息地。

在艺术中，树篱反映了社会经济历史。例如，19世纪画家John Ferneley的作品不仅描绘了贵族狩猎场景，还无意中展现了当时经济衰退的乡村景象——树木被砍作柴火，树篱稀疏破败。树篱在艺术和现实中都是一个变化的实体，体现了英格兰乡村的历史变迁。

Notebooks
The art of the hedgerow
April 28, 2025
Richard Negus
Themes:
Art, History
The hedgerow is never truly permanent. The hedge in art reflects the hedge in reality, a shifting entity, a feature that is sometimes lost and sometimes replaced.
Alfred Glendening's Picking Wild Flowers in the Hedgerow. Credit: Artepics / Alamy Stock Photo
It is often quoted that, since 1945, 50 per cent of English hedgerows have ‘disappeared’ from the landscape. Environmental campaigners correlate their thorny absence, and the habitat, food and connectivity they provided, with Britain’s decline in biodiversity. In the immediate aftermath of the Second World War, farmers were commanded by the Ministry of Food to maximise production. Agricultural rationalisation was deemed essential if Britain, desiccated by seven years of war, was to rid itself of rationing. The hedgerow was viewed by the technocrats as a hindrance to crop production. Any negative impact that such wholesale reductions might bring to wildlife was brutally ignored by the Labour government of
Clement Attlee
. Humans came first, and English humans were hungry.
Machines and munitions were repurposed. In field corners, military explosives splintered craggy elms and ancient oaks to shards. The bulldozers that had cleared barbed-wire emplacements in Normandy now eradicated English ribbons of thorn, spindle and hazel. The 1947 Agriculture Act was mercilessly effective in bringing about unprecedented agricultural efficiencies, particularly in arable production. A mere year after the Act’s passing, bread, flour and potatoes were removed from the ration book. By 1954, rationing itself became history. Yet
farming’s industrialisation
, so effective at ending postwar privation, was equally successful at effacing the English hedgerow.
However, the truth about hedges is not so cut and dried. Certainly, photographic evidence proves that many English hedgerows growing in 1939 were eradicated by government diktat after 1945 and into the early 1980s. Yet this most recent loss is no anomaly, and to understand the story of the humble hedgerow is to begin to understand the history of rural England.
The hedge has always been a fluctuating landscape feature, ebbing and flowing on the tide of agricultural requirements and the vagaries of the wider economy. Hedgerows are a man-made construct, an agricultural tool, utilising shrubby woodland sub-species. Such shrubs, when grown from seed, or transplanted as saplings and then planted in tight-knit staggered rows, grow into linear thorny belts. When these planted belts are subsequently laid or coppiced to increase basal density, and then the ensuing regrowth is regularly trimmed, they become the hedges so readily recognised.
British farmers have used hedges, on and off, since at least 2,500 BC as a means of retaining and providing shelter for livestock, as a wind break for crops or delineating the boundaries of land ownership. Hedgerows play a vital role in providing food and protection to a staggering variety of bird, mammal and invertebrate species. The hedge is as much a part of farming as the tractor, seed drill or plough.
The hedgerow’s ability to provide a fascinating and unexpectedly accurate guide to English socio-economic history can be told through the medium of art, particularly sporting art.
John Ferneley
(1782-1860) was a Leicestershire artist, beloved by the ‘Meltonians’, who made a pilgrimage to Melton Mowbray each hunting season from smart London addresses. They delighted in testing their nerves and necks, riding with hounds across the grass country of the East Midland Shires.
These men were the cream of early-Victorian society; Guy Paget notes that they were ‘rich, cultured and refined’, far removed from the hard-drinking, hard-riding local hunting squires of the preceding Georgian generation. The art these scarlet-clad effetes favoured was realistic and specific. A hefty commission was on offer for any artist who could faithfully depict a patron’s dearest horse, hound, friends, and the landscape across which they galloped.
John Ferneley was just such an artist
, and his account books testify both to the aristocratic pedigrees of his client base and the money they were prepared to pay for his work. Two such pieces, ‘Hunting In Croxton Park’ (1824) and ‘Melton Mowbray’ (1820) hang side-by-side today in the delightful galleries of the British Sporting Arts Trust (BSAT) at Palace House in Newmarket. Both picture the Meltonians in their full flight and sumptuous equestrian splendour.
Yet if one looks past the thoroughbred horses, well-cut coats and toppers and into the middle ground of the paintings, it is all too easy to see that Ferneley’s countryside of the 1820s was one laid low by recession. The trees the riders pass under are pollarded, their limbs hacked off for firewood by the local tenantry and labourers. data.title: The Signal Chat Leak and the NSA
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 美国国家安全顾问迈克·沃尔茨暗示，安全通讯应用Signal存在安全漏洞，并质疑《大西洋》主编杰弗里·戈尔德堡是否通过技术手段入侵了他发起的群聊。与此同时，美国国家安全局（NSA）曾发布报告警告Signal存在漏洞。NSA面临两难选择：是利用这些漏洞监视他国，还是修复它们以保护美国通信安全。Signal广泛用于各类人群和机构，包括美国军方。若NSA选择不公开漏洞并被他人发现，可能反被用于攻击美国。此外，智能手机本身也存在被间谍软件入侵的风险，特别是个人设备不适合处理机密政府通信。NSA必须平衡保护美国通信和监控外国信息的双重任务。

43844557.article_content:
The Signal Chat Leak and the NSA
US National Security Advisor Mike Waltz, who started the now-infamous group chat coordinating a US attack against the Yemen-based Houthis on March 15, is seemingly now suggesting that the secure messaging service Signal has security vulnerabilities.
"I didn’t see this loser in the group," Waltz
told
Fox News about
Atlantic
editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg, whom Waltz
invited
to the chat. "Whether he did it deliberately or it happened in some other technical mean, is something we’re trying to figure out."
Waltz’s implication that Goldberg may have hacked his way in was followed by a
report
from CBS News that the US National Security Agency (NSA) had sent out a bulletin to its employees last month warning them about a security "vulnerability" identified in Signal.
The truth, however, is much more interesting. If Signal has vulnerabilities, then China, Russia, and other US adversaries suddenly have a new incentive to discover them. At the same time, the NSA urgently needs to find and fix any vulnerabilities quickly as it can—and similarly, ensure that commercial smartphones are free of backdoors—access points that allow people other than a smartphone’s user to bypass the usual security authentication methods to access the device’s contents.
That is essential for anyone who wants to keep their communications private, which should be all of us.
It’s common knowledge
that the NSA’s mission is breaking into and eavesdropping on other countries’ networks. (During President George W. Bush’s administration, the NSA conducted warrantless taps into domestic communications as well—surveillance that
several
district courts
ruled
to be illegal before those decisions were later
overturned
by appeals courts. To this day, many legal experts
maintain
that the program violated federal privacy protections.) But the organization has a secondary, complementary responsibility: to protect US communications from others who want to spy on them. That is to say: While one part of the NSA is listening into foreign communications, another part is stopping foreigners from doing the same to Americans.
Those missions never contradicted during the Cold War, when allied and enemy communications were wholly separate. Today, though, everyone uses the same computers, the same software, and the same networks. That creates a tension.
When the NSA discovers a technological vulnerability in a service such as Signal (or buys one on the thriving clandestine vulnerability market), does it exploit it in secret, or reveal it so that it can be fixed? Since at least 2014, a US government interagency
"equities" process
has been used to decide whether it is in the national interest to take advantage of a particular security flaw, or to fix it. The trade-offs are often complicated and hard.
Waltz—along with Vice President J.D. Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and the other officials in the Signal group—have just made the trade-offs much tougher to resolve. Signal is both widely available and widely used. Smaller governments that can’t afford their own military-grade encryption use it. Journalists, human rights workers, persecuted minorities, dissidents, corporate executives, and criminals around the world use it. Many of these populations are of great interest to the NSA.
At the same time, as we have now discovered, the app is being used for operational US military traffic. So, what does the NSA do if it finds a security flaw in Signal?
Previously, it might have preferred to keep the flaw quiet and use it to listen to adversaries. Now, if the agency does that, it risks someone else finding the same vulnerability and using it against the US government. And if it was later disclosed that the NSA could have fixed the problem and didn’t, then the results might be catastrophic for the agency.
Smartphones present a similar trade-off. The biggest risk of eavesdropping on a Signal conversation comes from the individual phones that the app is running on. While it’s largely unclear whether the US officials involved had downloaded the app onto personal or government-issued phones—although Witkoff suggested on X that the program was on his "
personal devices
"—smartphones are consumer devices, not at all suitable for classified US government conversations. An entire industry of spyware companies sells capabilities to remotely hack smartphones for any country willing to pay. More capable countries have more sophisticated operations. Just last year, attacks that were later attributed to China
attempted
to access both President Donald Trump and Vance’s smartphones. Previously, the FBI—as well as
law enforcement agencies in other countries
—have pressured both Apple and Google to add "backdoors" in their phones to more easily facilitate court-authorized eavesdropping.

data.article_summary: 本文回顾了4chan网站的历史及其对互联网文化的深远影响。4chan由青少年Christopher Poole于2003年创立，借鉴了日本留言板2channel的格式，允许用户匿名发布各种内容，包括色情、盗版文件和政治言论。该网站早期因其无拘无束的特性成为网络“垃圾帖”的发源地，并孕育了独特的网络俚语和 trolling 文化。然而，随着社交媒体的发展，4chan逐渐失去影响力，并在2015年被出售。2023年4月，4chan遭到黑客攻击并短暂下线，复原后其源代码和版主账户被泄露。尽管4chan曾是网络亚文化和极端言论的温床，但如今其他平台如Truth Social和Parler等也在传播类似内容。4chan推动了网络文化的加速发展，其“玩世不恭的厌世态度”影响了如今的网络话语模式，甚至渗透到最高权力层。

主要讨论点：对4chan及类似网络平台的影响、演变及匿名性的看法

不同观点：
• ViktorRay认为，4chan等网站在2000年代末和2010年代初只是小众、地下、傻气的网站，用户并未预料到它们会对现实世界产生影响。他对如今主流媒体如《纽约客》报道4chan感到不可思议，认为这些网站最初只是供用户发布无意义内容的地方，而非影响现实世界的平台。

• Discordian93回忆了4chan上特定板块（如/vp/）的昔日盛况，对网站的现状感到惋惜，表达了对4chan演变过程的感慨。

• Yeul强调了互联网匿名性的重要性，怀念过去网络身份与现实身份分离的时代。他认为，匿名性在某些情况下仍然有其价值，例如避免潜在的职业风险。

• user9999999999的观点较为简短，指出用户只是转移到了其他平台，暗示4chan的影响力和用户可能已经迁移到其他地方。

• tiahura以幽默的方式回应，提到使用4chan等网站的实际好处，如寻找优惠券，以此表达对网站实用性的认可。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是4chan等网站在现实世界中的影响。ViktorRay对这种影响的意外性表示惊讶，而其他用户更多关注网站的变化和昔日的回忆。

• 匿名性是另一个值得注意的讨论点。Yeul特别强调了匿名性在网络使用中的重要性，并暗示这种特性在当今社会仍有其价值。

• 用户对4chan等网站从地下、小众平台发展到对现实世界产生影响的过程表达了不同的感慨和看法，反映了网络文化演变的复杂性。

• 部分用户提到了网站内容和用户群体的变迁，暗示平台在不同时间段的特色和用户体验可能发生了显著变化。

4chan was where I learned that the internet could be bad. I first encountered the site during high school, not long after its founding, in 2003, by an American teen-ager named Christopher Poole (better known by his username, moot). Poole copied the format of a Japanese message board nicknamed 2channel; users on 4chan could anonymously post an unfiltered mix of text, images, and animated
GIF
s. Illicit material was never hard to find on the internet, but 4chan served as an early hub—or “dumping ground” might be more apt. The site was inundated with pornography, pirated files, and uncensored screeds about dating or politics. Its background, a pale yellow gradient, still gives me a slight frisson, like a
Playboy
issue hidden under the bed. I would often test the censorship settings on a library or school computer’s
LAN
internet connection by trying to load 4chan. Usually, it wouldn’t work, which hinted at the site’s infamy: even the grown-ups knew at least its name, and that it warranted a place on ban lists.
On 4chan, usernames were most often just “Anonymous” or a string of numbers. I never posted, but I understood the appeal of hiding behind a mask and becoming one of a crowd. The site formed a collective id that could be called up in a web browser, years before the digital gang wars of Twitter began. Learning the forum’s slang was the key to understanding its jokes: lulz, fren, TFW, troll. Posts were deleted when they stopped getting new engagement, which typically happened quickly, especially if the messages failed to provoke. At a time when the internet was still sparsely populated, 4chan guaranteed constant energy, no matter the time of day or night. But as the social-media landscape grew up around it, during the twenty-tens, and other sites competed as spaces for “shitposting,” that digital term of art, 4chan faded in relevance. In 2015, Poole sold it to the owner of 2channel, the Japanese site that had inspired it. It survived as a basement of the internet—dingy, subterranean, and in a state of arrested development—which is why it wasn’t exactly surprising when, on April 14th, 4chan suddenly disappeared. A spinoff forum called Soyjak.party (even harsher and more political than its predecessor) took credit for hacking the site and shutting it down.
After a week and a half, 4chan limped back online over the weekend, but an air of embarrassment hung over its return. The hackers had leaked 4chan’s source code, along with the accounts of its anonymous volunteer moderators. “It’s pretty archaic internet infrastructure,” Jared Holt, a researcher at the Institute for Strategic Dialogue focussing on domestic extremist movements on the web, told me. Rather than an act of total destruction, the hack appeared to be a troll, a dig at 4chan’s secondary status two decades into the forum’s existence. Once a digital home to political incorrectness, and a staging ground for incel culture, white-power groups, mass-shooting manifestos, and more, 4chan is now one among many platforms just as conducive to hate speech. President Donald Trump’s own Truth Social is another, as is Parler, the right-wing video site offering “True Freedom.” There’s Patriots Win, a kind of Trump-focussed Reddit clone; Kiwi Farm, a hub known for coördinated online harassment; and X, which under the ownership of Elon Musk has loosened content-moderation policies and allowed the kind of conspiracy theories and graphic imagery that once thrived on 4chan. As Holt put it, “4chan had essentially been outflanked to the right.”
What’s undeniable is that 4chan helped form the content ecosystem as we know it. The kind of real-time one-upmanship that happens on X, TikTok, and video podcasts; the culture of “owns,” clapbacks, and online putdowns—all of it crystallized on 4chan. The site demonstrated, before many people realized it, that the internet existed fundamentally in a Hobbesian state of nature, hosting a war of all against all. Cole Stryker, an editorial consultant in Los Angeles and the author of “
Epic Win for Anonymous: How 4chan’s Army Conquered the Web
,” from 2011, summed up the forum’s influential attitude as “nonstop playful misanthropy.” 4chan played a role in the acceleration of digital culture, the onslaught of discourse in the form of a million multimedia particles. On 4chan, “it was just as easy to share an image as it was to share words,” Stryker told me, adding, “Now everyone kind of has that capability to speak in that language.” Today, a fluency in memes extends to the highest levels of authority. “Even our President and our Vice-President are posters,” Stryker said. The official White House account on X, in particular, has taken on a trolling aspect; one A.I.-generated image it posted in March, of the arrest of an alleged drug dealer in the anime style of
Studio Ghibli

data.title: Microsoft announces new European digital commitments
data.author: mweibel
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟的自主权与技术供应链，特别是云计算和数据主权问题。

不同观点：
• **cadamsdotcom**：主张欧盟需要在每个供应链环节上审视其自主能力，包括从原材料到数字通讯的各个方面。强调必须考虑储备、关系稳定性、航运通道等多重因素。同时指出，重启被忽视的技术和供应链虽然困难，但将带来巨大创新潜力。这个过程类似于在美国建设高速铁路的难度，但非常必要。

• **benterix**：质疑美国大型云服务提供商（如微软的Azure）在欧盟建立数据中心的真正意图。认为即便这些公司提供“欧洲云”，用户是否会买账仍是个问题。核心关切是，欧洲希望在政治、经济和隐私方面完全独立于美国，而美国公司控制下的数据中心可能无法实现这一目标，尤其是考虑到Azure的安全性问题。

• **ForHackernews**：对“主权云”的定义提出疑问。认为如果微软控制着运行在欧盟数据中心的Azure软件，那么这些数据中心是否真的“主权”值得怀疑，因为控制权仍然在美国公司手中。

补充讨论：
• **HelloUsername**：提到微软承诺保护其在欧洲的业务，这可能与主权云和数据安全问题相关，但未深入展开。

争议焦点：
• 欧盟是否能够以及如何实现技术供应链的自主权，特别是在云计算领域。
• 美国大型科技公司在欧盟建立数据中心是否能真正实现欧洲的“数据主权”目标。
• “主权云”的定义和实际控制权问题，即如果软件仍由美国公司控制，那么这些数据中心是否真的主权。

总结：讨论围绕欧盟在技术供应链和云计算领域的自主权展开，各方对如何实现真正的“主权云”以及美国科技巨头的参与表示了不同看法和疑虑。

data.title: Programming languages should have a tree traversal primitive
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
Tyler Glaiel在博客中建议编程语言应加入一种树遍历原语（tree traversal primitive），类似于用于线性遍历的for/foreach循环。这种结构可以帮助开发者更简便地处理树状数据结构，避免手动编写递归函数，提升代码可读性和减少错误。

他提出的`for_tree`语法类似于传统的for循环，但能够处理树的分支遍历。其结构包括初始化、条件判断和分支处理。相比手动递归，`for_tree`更直观，且支持break、continue和return等控制流操作，甚至还可加入"prune"操作来阻止遍历某些分支。

Glaiel认为，这种原语比基于范围的for循环更灵活，无需预先定义迭代器，适用于内存中不存在或动态生成的树结构。不过，他也提醒使用时需注意潜在的性能问题，如生成不必要的分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效地遍历和操作复杂数据结构（如树和图），是否需要更好的原语或工具支持。

不同观点：
• aeonik：支持引入更好的原语，如Optics（透镜、棱镜、遍历）、Zippers（拉链数据结构）和查询语言（如SPARQL、Datalog、Cypher、Prolog），以实现对数据结构的局部编辑和语义遍历。
• Xmd5a：支持使用Clojure的`clojure.walk`等现有工具进行树遍历，并引用Perlis原则，认为应优先考虑对单一数据结构进行多功能操作。
• pgt：推荐使用Clojure的Specter库进行数据导航和转换，强调其性能和类型保留的优势。
• swiftcoder：认为问题在于"在C++中编写迭代器比应有的要难"，并提供Python生成器作为示例，指出无需将整个树加载到内存中。
• jerf：认为这是"特定种类的迭代器"，可以通过任何支持迭代器的语言实现，并提供Python示例。
• yxhuvud：反对语言的过度复杂化，主张通过内部迭代器使数据结构自行添加所需逻辑。
• monkeyelite：认为C++的迭代器已经解决了这个问题，基本操作如前进和解除引用可以通过迭代器实现。
• ivanjermakov：认为函数式语言通过Foldable或Traversable类型类很好地处理了这个问题。
• pmontra：指出在高级语言（如Python和Ruby）中，树等复杂数据结构的使用较少，常用的是数组和哈希表。
• JaumeGreen：设想一种具有更多数据结构和易于遍历工具的语言，但也提到可能需要更好的文献和培训来处理现有数据类型。
• Retr0id：指出递归函数在处理大树时的栈深度限制问题，建议使用自定义栈结构。
• soegaard：建议选择允许定义自己控制结构的语言进行实践，如Racket、Scheme、Rust。
• cdrini：认为标准库对图（通用树）的支持可以帮助图在编程中更常用，并介绍了自己的项目gstd。
• jpmonettas：提到Clojure已经有`tree-seq`用于树遍历。
• drbojingle：偏题，提到编程语言需要维度分析以避免单位错误。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否需要引入新的语言原语或工具来处理树和图的遍历和操作。一些参与者支持引入更高级别的工具和库（如Optics、Zippers、Specter），而另一些参与者认为现有的迭代器和递归函数已经足够，或者可以通过内部迭代器和控制结构解决。
• 讨论中涉及多种语言和工具，包括Clojure、Haskell、Python、C++、Ruby、Racket、Rust等，展示了不同语言社区对该问题的处理方式。
• 有人提到高级语言中树的使用较少，更多使用数组和哈希表，而低级语言可能更需要树遍历的支持。

• soegaard：建议选择允许定义自己控制结构的语言进行实践，如Racket、Scheme、Rust。
• cdrini：认为标准库对图（通用树）的支持可以帮助图在编程中更常用，并介绍了自己的项目gstd。
• jpmonettas：提到Clojure已经有`tree-seq`用于树遍历。
• drbojingle：偏题，提到编程语言需要维度分析以避免单位错误。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否需要引入新的语言原语或工具来处理树和图的遍历和操作。一些参与者支持引入更高级别的工具和库（如Optics、Zippers、Specter），而另一些参与者认为现有的迭代器和递归函数已经足够，或者可以通过内部迭代器和控制结构解决。
• 讨论中涉及多种语言和工具，包括Clojure、Haskell、Python、C++、Ruby、Racket、Rust等，展示了不同语言社区对该问题的处理方式。
• 有人提到高级语言中树的使用较少，更多使用数组和哈希表，而低级语言可能更需要树遍历的支持。

data.title: Groups move for disclosure of Chemours' sealed PFAS documents
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 环境组织通过南方环境法律中心向法院提交动议，要求公开 Chemours 公司及其前身杜邦公司试图密封的约 21,000 页文件。这些文件涉及 Chemours 位于布拉登县工厂的 PFAS（全氟及多氟烷基物质）污染问题，对当地社区的健康和财产价值造成影响。PFAS 是一类持久性化学物质，与免疫功能减弱、癌症风险增加等问题有关。尽管 Chemours 计划扩大其 PFAS 生产，但仍试图隐瞒相关文件，引发公众质疑。此前，公共事业和地方政府已起诉该公司，要求赔偿因 PFAS 排放造成的损失。环保组织认为，这些文件至关重要，应公开以保护公众利益。

By Trisha Talton, Coastal Review
The chemical manufacturing company that has publicly touted its products, business strategies and chemistries in ad campaigns aimed at polishing its image will further harm North Carolinians if it is successful in keeping thousands of pages of documents sealed in court, environmental organizations argue. The Southern Environmental Law Center on Monday filed a court motion to intervene in a case brought against Chemours and its predecessor company DuPont, attorneys for which have asked the court to keep up to 21,000 pages of documents under seal.
The Southern Environmental Law Center on Monday filed a court motion to intervene in a case brought against Chemours and its predecessor company DuPont, attorneys for which have asked the court to keep up to 21,000 pages of documents under seal.
Those documents, SELC argues in its motion, “will help communities understand the harm the facility has caused, and will continue to cause, to their own health, their property values, and even the lives of future generations.” The motion was filed on behalf of Cape Fear River Watch, the North Carolina Coastal Federation, which publishes Coastal Review, and the Environmental Justice Community Action Network in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina.
In February, attorneys for Chemours and DuPont requested the court keep from public view what they say are mostly internal communications between company employees about “non-public facts” that pertain, in part, to chemical production and is therefore “competitively sensitive.” An attorney with Brooks Pierce Law Firm, which represents public utilities and local governments downstream of Chemours’ Bladen County plant, told Coastal Review last month that many of the documents in question are already on public record. Brooks Pierce was expected on Monday to respond to the companies’ motion to keep the documents under seal. A lawyer with the firm did not respond to a request for comment by the time of this publication.
Cape Fear Public Utility Authority, Brunswick County, Lower Cape Fear Water & Sewer Authority and Wrightsville Beach in October 2017 sued the companies to recover costs and damages associated with Fayetteville Works’ plant’s discharges of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or PFAS, for decades into the Cape Fear River, the drinking water supply for tens of thousands of residents in the region.
PFAS are a group of more than 14,000 chemicals used in everyday consumer products including food containers, stain-resistant carpet and water-repellant gear. These human-made chemical compounds are persistent in the environment and have been found to accumulate in people and animals. Exposure to these substances has been linked to weakened immune function, reproductive and developmental issues and increased risk of some cancers.
After intentionally hiding their toxic PFAS pollution for decades, Chemours and DuPont now want to conceal essential information that directly affects the lives of half-a-million people,” SELC Senior Attorney Jean Zhuang said in a release Monday. “And Chemours has the audacity to try to hide thousands of pages of information as the company plans to expand its PFAS manufacturing operations. data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 一项由伦敦卫生与热带医学学院和帝国理工学院进行的研究显示，行人和骑自行车者被SUV等大型车辆撞到的死亡风险比被普通轿车撞到高44%，儿童的这一风险更是高达82%。研究分析了过去35年中的68万多起交通事故，发现SUV因其较高的前端设计，会导致更高的撞击点和更大的二次伤害风险。SUV在英国新车注册中占比已达三分之一，其流行对道路安全和环保目标构成威胁。研究建议通过政策 discourage 大型车辆的使用，并投资建设更安全的交通基础设施。
